# Sacred Gear Lua API reference

Everything a mod can call, by area: functions, options, fields and events. It is generated from the LuaLS annotations
in `gear/meta/` (how to change them: `docs/Development.md`, "The Lua API annotations"). The guide to writing a mod
(install, `mod.lua`, events, the file overlay, the mod manager, automation, examples) is [Gear.md](Gear.md).

## Editor support (Lua Language Server)

`gear/meta/*.lua` are [LuaLS](https://luals.github.io/) definition files (`---@meta`): they declare the `gear` global,
the objects it returns, the events and callbacks, the options tables, and the manifest of `mod.lua`. With them the
editor completes and checks mod code (VS Code with the "Lua" extension by sumneko, or any editor with LuaLS).

In this repository nothing is needed: `.luarc.json` at the root points LuaLS at `gear/meta`, so the examples in
`gear/examples` get completion and checks.

**Without this repository: the MDK.** `gear/dist/mdk` (generated, committed) and each release has `sacred-gear-mdk.zip`, a mod development kit built from
`gear/meta` by `tools/gen_gear_mdk.py` (so it is always current): the definitions, this reference, `Gear.md`, a mod
template, a few examples and scripts to create and pack a mod. Extract it, open the folder in VS Code and run
`tools/new-mod.ps1`; `.luarc.json` is already set up.

**In a mod repository** (for instance `sacred-gear-mods`, next to a checkout of this one): copy
`gear/meta/luarc.template.json` to `.luarc.json` in the root of the mod repository and set `workspace.library` to the
`gear/meta` folder (a relative path from that root, or an absolute one). That is all.

What the template sets besides the library:

- `runtime.version` is `LuaJIT`, the Lua Sacred Gear runs.
- `runtime.builtin` hides the libraries a mod does not get: `io`, `debug`, `package`, `jit`, `ffi`, `utf8`, `bit32`, and
  `os`, which `gear/meta/gear.lua` declares again with the four functions mods have (`clock`, `time`, `date`,
  `difftime`). The basic functions a mod lacks (`load`, `loadstring`, `loadfile`, `dofile`, `collectgarbage`,
  `getfenv`, `setfenv`, `newproxy`, `gcinfo`) are declared there as deprecated, so the editor strikes them through.
  What a mod has: `assert error ipairs next pairs pcall rawequal rawget rawset select setmetatable getmetatable
  tonumber tostring type unpack xpcall`, `_VERSION`, `print` and `require` (its own files only), `string`, `table`,
  `math`, `bit`, `coroutine`, and `gear`.

In `mod.lua`, annotate the returned table for completion of the manifest keys:

```lua
---@type GearModManifest
return {
    id = 'hello',
    name = 'Hello, Sacred Gear',
    version = '1.0',
}
```

Handlers get typed arguments from `gear.on`:

```lua
gear.on('frame', function(dt)            -- dt: number
    local hero = gear.world.hero()       -- Creature?
    if hero then print(hero:hp(), hero:class()) end
end)
gear.on('draw', function(state)          -- state: GearUiState
    if state.mode ~= 'game' then return end
    gear.ui.text('Hello', 24, 24, {color = 0xFFFFD080, shadow = true})
end)
```

Not covered by the annotations: values a mod gets from a custom event (`gear.emit` and its handlers take `...`), keys
of `gear.config` (declare your own with `---@type {my_setting: number}` on a local), and the runtime rule that
`gear.auto` exists only in automation runs.

## The gear global

### GearEventName

| Value | |
|---|---|
| `'load'` | All mods are loaded. |
| `'frame'` | Every in-game frame. |
| `'draw'` | After the frame handlers, to draw the UI. |
| `'idle'` | Automation only: every 50 ms in the menus. |
| `'unload'` | The player switched this mod off in the mod manager: clean up (handlers, timers and the rest are dropped after it). |
| `'settings.changed'` | A setting of this mod changed: `(id, value)`. |
| `'session.start'` | A game with a hero runs. |
| `'session.stop'` | That hero is gone. |
| `'game.saved'` | A save `gear.game.save` asked for is written. |
| `'savegame.changed'` | The game loaded a savegame or hero file, or started a new game: `(kind, scope, number)` (see `gear.savegame`). |
| `'savegame.leaving'` | Another savegame is loading (or a new game starts) and the running one ends: `(scope, kind)`; the data kept for `scope` can still be written with `gear.savegame.write_saved`. Fires before `savegame.changed`. |
| `'savegame.saving'` | A savegame was written and the data of the running game is about to be kept for it: `(scope)`; write what changed now. |
| `'game.save_failed'` | It could not be written. |
| `'game.saved_other'` | A save the game or the player made: the quicksave, the savegame window, the game's own Auto-Save. |
| `'game.hero_saved'` | The game wrote the hero file (`Save\HeroNN.pax`): `(slot, network)`. A network game does this every 5 minutes, when the player leaves and at merchants; the moment an item or gold that changed hands is safe in the player's own save. |
| `'kill'` | A kill the local computer sent to the game (a hero's kill: `(kill)`, see `GearKill`). |
| `'mp_message'` | A message of the mod channel (`gear.mp.send`) arrived: `(from, channel, payload)`. |
| `'net_caps'` | The custom net messages became available, or the list of players who can use them changed (gear.net): `(caps)`, see `GearNetCaps`. |
| `'chat.line'` | The game added a chat or message line: `(line)`, see `GearChatLine` (gear.chat). |
| `'party.control'` | `gear.party.control` gave the player another hero: `(from, to)` (creatures). |
| `'buff.applied'` | A mod gave a creature a Gear buff: `(creature, key, id, strength)`. |
| `'buff.ended'` | A Gear buff ended (its time ran out, it was removed, a savegame was loaded): `(creature, key, id)`. |
| `'realm.changed'` | `gear.realm.use` switched the online play server: `(realm)`. |
| `'combat.constant'` | The engine loads a pooled float constant inside its own code (hit handlers, difficulty factors ...); a handler may return another number for it. |
| `'skillslot.key'` | A character key reached the skill slot window; a handler routes it to a slot (`slot` or `{slot, 'select'}`), `false` ignores it. |
| `'combat.branch'` | A conditional jump in the hit handlers and a few other functions: a handler may decide whether it is taken (`name`, `vanilla`, `index`, the compared `eax`). |
| `'skillslot.select'` | A digit key selected a skill slot of the HUD (`index`: which of the five places in the key handler). |
| `'bonus.constant'` | A number the item bonus code pushes as the argument of a random roll or a text lookup; a handler may return another. |
| `'drops.roll'` | A creature's loot function is about to run; a handler may change the rarity bonus or return false to cancel the roll. |
| `'drops.select'` | The loot function asks the equipment type picker for an item; a handler may change the category, level or quality, or name the item type. |
| `'effect.add'` | The engine adds a value to a creature's effect entry; a handler may decide what is stored (see `GearEffectAdd`). |
| `'damage'` | The final damage of a hit, before the engine applies it; a handler may return another damage (16 bit, 0 to 65534). |
| `'ability.hit'` | A hit of a creature that has a combat art or spell (or a copy, ids from 100) in flight: `(attacker, victim, art, damage)`; `art` is the id the hero used (a copy's own id). |
| `'ability.route'` | A hero has a combat art in flight and the engine asks which class's code runs it: `(type, art, vanilla, action, id)`; return a hero type 1 to 9 or nil. |
| `'motion.select'` | A hero is about to play a motion slot: `(type, slot, id)`; return another slot (0 to 255) or nil. |
| `'rune.usable'` | A hero type is checked for the class mask of an ability (reading a rune): `(type, ability, vanilla)`; return true or false, or nil to leave it. |
| `'item.use'` | A potion is drunk: `(e)`, see `GearItemUse`; return `'consume'` (no effect, the potion is used up as ever), `'keep'` (no effect, the potion stays; the drinking sound plays) or nil (the engine's effect). Not asked while Lua code itself runs, so a drink a mod starts (`creature:drink_potion`) has the engine's effect. |
| `'creature.created'` | The engine's own code created a creature (a sector filled with its spawn table, a script, a respawn): `(e)`, see `GearCreatureCreated`. Delivered on the next tick, so the creature is complete. Not for creatures `gear.world.spawn` makes, nor for those a savegame loads. |
| `'creature.ability'` | The creature AI picks the ability (skill or spell id) a creature uses; a handler may return another id. |
| `'level.factor'` | The engine asks for the integer factor of a level (a hook inside its own code; the first handler that returns a number answers). |

### GearItemUse

A handler registered with `gear.on`; pass it to `gear.off` to remove it. What the `item.use` event gets: a potion is drunk.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `item` | `integer` | The potion's object id. |
| `type` | `integer` | The potion's item type. |
| `creature` | `integer` | The id of the creature that drinks it. |

### GearCreatureCreated

What the `creature.created` event gets.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `creature` | `Creature` | The new creature. |
| `id` | `integer` | Its object id. |
| `type` | `integer` | Its object type id. |
| `x` | `integer` | Where the engine placed it. |
| `y` | `integer` |  |
| `layer` | `integer` |  |

### GearHit

What the `damage` event gets.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `damage` | `integer` | The damage the engine computed (after the resistances, before it is applied). |
| `victim_type` | `integer` | Creature type of the one that is hit (-1: unknown). |
| `attacker_type` | `integer` | Creature type of the attacker (-1: none, e.g. a trap or an effect). |
| `site` | `integer` | Which damage hook site (0: the damage resolution of the hit handlers). |
| `victim` | `integer` | Object id of the one that is hit (0: unknown). |
| `attacker` | `integer` | Object id of the attacker (0: none). With `gear.world.object(id)` this tells which creature took part. |

### GearEffectAdd

What the `effect.add` event gets: the engine is adding to one entry of a creature's effect list.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `creature` | `integer` | The creature's id. |
| `ability` | `integer` | The ability the creature is using (its current skill or spell id). |
| `effect` | `integer` | The effect id of the entry the engine is at. |
| `flags` | `integer` | The creature's flag word (bits 0x4000000 and 0x20000000 mark stacking effects). |
| `counter` | `integer` | The creature's effect counter. |
| `value` | `number` | The new sum (the entry's value plus what is added). |
| `max` | `number` | The entry's maximum. |
| `current` | `number` | The entry's value now. |

### GearEffectAnswer

What a handler of `effect.add` answers; nil means the engine does its own store and clamps.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `number` | Store this in the entry; without it nothing is stored. (optional) |
| `effect` | `integer` | Change the next entry (from this one on) with this effect id instead of the engine's. (optional) |
| `clamp` | `boolean` | Apply the engine's clamps (default true): above the maximum becomes the maximum, below its floor becomes 0. (optional) |
| `finish` | `boolean` | Leave the function after this entry (default false: go on with the next). (optional) |
| `stack` | `'set'\|'inc'` | The creature's effect counter becomes 1 / grows by one. (optional) |

### GearHandler

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `event` | `string` | The event the handler listens to. |
| `fn` | `function` | The handler. |

### GearTimer

A timer started with `gear.after` or `gear.every`; pass it to `gear.cancel`. Opaque.

### GearModInfo

What `gear.mod` tells a mod about itself.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | The manifest's `id`. |
| `name` | `string` | The manifest's `name` (default: the id). |
| `version` | `string` | The manifest's `version` (default `'0'`). |
| `dir` | `string` | The mod's folder name under `mods`. |

### Gear

Reached as `gear`.

The `gear` global: Sacred Gear's API, one copy per mod (each mod has its own globals).

All mod code runs on the engine thread, between the game's update and the drawing of the frame, one handler at a time, so handlers see a consistent state and need no locks.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | `string` | Sacred Gear's version. |
| `mod` | `GearModInfo` | This mod's identity. |
| `config` | `table<string, any>` | This mod's settings: the manifest's `config`, overridden by `config.lua`. |
| `data` | `GearData` | The engine's data tables (read only, except the abilities and regions). |
| `text` | `GearText` | The game's texts by id. |
| `files` | `GearFiles` | The mod's file overlay. |
| `hooks` | `GearHooks` | The engine hooks that ask mods for values. |
| `json` | `GearJson` | JSON encoding and decoding. |
| `pipe` | `GearPipeModule` | Named pipe clients. |
| `world` | `GearWorld` | The world: hero, creatures, items, spawning, pickup rules. |
| `drops` | `GearDrops` | Item drops: chance, rarity weights, the generator, the roll and select events. |
| `inv` | `GearInv` | Inventories: containers, items, export and import of items. |
| `game` | `GearGame` | The game itself: difficulty and saving. |
| `chat` | `GearChat` | The game's chat and message lines: who sent them, the session's history, the game's overlay. |
| `clipboard` | `GearClipboard` | The Windows clipboard: copy text out of the game. |
| `realm` | `GearRealmApi` | The online play server (realms): list, switch, add. |
| `party` | `GearParty` | Companion heroes in single player: recruit, switch control, orders. |
| `buffs` | `GearBuffs` | Buffs, debuffs and auras on any creature: combat values for a while, with the game's spell overlays. |
| `classes` | `GearClasses` | Custom hero classes: the tier of each art for each body, ability copies, hero skills. |
| `models` | `GearModels` | The models' motion slots (which clips a body has, giving it another's). |
| `lookup` | `GearLookup` | Finding things of the game (items, creatures, abilities, a mod's own kinds) by a few letters, with a picker window. |
| `fmt` | `GearFmt` | Numbers, times and texts made ready to show (thousands, clocks, cut to a length, markup removed). |
| `toast` | `GearToast` | Short messages that stack up on the screen and fade; the layout editor moves them. |
| `events` | `GearEvents` | Hooks between mods: declare the custom events the mod emits, list what is declared. |
| `savegame` | `GearSavegame` | The savegame being played: its scope, and the mod's files that belong to it. |
| `store` | `GearStore` | The mod's own data in JSON files of its folder: load with defaults, save, save when changed. |
| `mp` | `GearMp` | Players of a network game, the host, the mod channel and the `kill` event. |
| `net` | `GearNet` | Custom net messages: named channels between computers and the game server. |
| `settings` | `GearSettings` | This mod's settings (declared in `mod.lua`, changed by the player in the mod manager). |
| `keys` | `GearKeys` | This mod's declared key binds. |
| `input` | `GearInput` | The game's own keys, remapped. |
| `mods` | `GearMods` | The installed mods; a page of this mod's own in the mod manager. |
| `menu` | `GearMenu` | Menus mods add items to (the game menu) and the mod that draws them. |
| `ui` | `GearUi` | Drawing on top of the game, widgets, panels and the layout. |
| `auto` | `GearAuto` | Automation (only with `-gear-auto` and `automation = true` in `mod.lua`). (optional) |

#### `gear.on(event, fn) -> GearHandler`

Calls `fn` for `event`; returns a handle for `gear.off`. Built-in events: see `GearEventName`. Any other name is a custom event that `gear.emit` fires (it has a dot: `twitch.command`).

Forms:

- `fun(event: 'load', fn: fun()): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'frame', fn: fun(dt: number)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'draw', fn: fun(state: GearUiState)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'idle', fn: fun()): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'unload', fn: fun()): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'settings.changed', fn: fun(id: string, value: boolean|number|string)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'session.start', fn: fun(hero: Creature)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'session.stop', fn: fun()): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'game.saved', fn: fun(slot: integer, info: GearSaveInfo)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'game.save_failed', fn: fun(slot: integer, message: string)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'game.saved_other', fn: fun(slot: integer)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'savegame.changed', fn: fun(kind: 'load'|'hero'|'new', scope: string?, number: integer)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'savegame.leaving', fn: fun(scope: string?, kind: 'load'|'hero'|'new')): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'savegame.saving', fn: fun(scope: string)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'game.hero_saved', fn: fun(slot: integer, network: boolean)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'kill', fn: fun(kill: GearKill)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'mp_message', fn: fun(from: GearPlayer, channel: string, payload: table|string)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'net_caps', fn: fun(caps: GearNetCaps)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'chat.line', fn: fun(line: GearChatLine)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'party.control', fn: fun(from: Creature, to: Creature)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'buff.applied', fn: fun(creature: Creature?, key: string, id: string, strength: number)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'buff.ended', fn: fun(creature: Creature?, key: string, id: string)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'realm.changed', fn: fun(realm: GearRealm)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'combat.constant', fn: fun(name: string, vanilla: number, index: integer): number?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'skillslot.key', fn: fun(character: integer): (integer|false|{[1]: integer, [2]: 'full'|'select'})?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'combat.branch', fn: fun(name: string, vanilla: boolean, index: integer, eax: integer): boolean?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'skillslot.select', fn: fun(index: integer)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'bonus.constant', fn: fun(index: integer, vanilla: number, address: integer): number?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'drops.roll', fn: fun(ev: GearDropRoll): boolean?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'drops.select', fn: fun(ev: GearDropSelect)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'effect.add', fn: fun(e: GearEffectAdd): GearEffectAnswer?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'damage', fn: fun(hit: GearHit): integer?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'ability.hit', fn: fun(attacker: Creature, victim: Creature, art: integer, damage: integer)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'ability.route', fn: fun(type: integer, art: integer, vanilla: integer, action: integer, id: integer): integer?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'motion.select', fn: fun(type: integer, slot: integer, id: integer): integer?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'rune.usable', fn: fun(type: integer, ability: integer, vanilla: boolean): boolean?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'item.use', fn: fun(e: GearItemUse): ('consume'|'keep')?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'creature.created', fn: fun(e: GearCreatureCreated)): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'creature.ability', fn: fun(type: integer, vanilla: integer, index: integer, address: integer): integer?): GearHandler`
- `fun(event: 'level.factor', fn: fun(level: number, site: integer): number?): GearHandler`

- `event`: `string`
- `fn`: `fun(...: any)`
- returns `GearHandler`

#### `gear.off(handle)`

Removes a handler.

- `handle`: `GearHandler`

#### `gear.emit(event, ...)`

Calls every handler of a custom event now. Custom names have a dot (`twitch.command`); the built-in events and the prefixes `session.`, `gear.`, `pipe.`, `game.`, `chat.` and `settings.` are reserved. Handlers may emit events too, up to 8 levels deep. Handlers of `prefix.*` (`gear.on('bounty.*', fn)`) also get every custom event below the prefix, with the event name first. See `gear.events` for publishing hooks.

- `event`: `string`
- `...`: `any`

#### `gear.after(seconds, fn) -> GearTimer`

Runs `fn` once after `seconds` (real seconds while the game runs frames, not in menus or loading screens).

- `seconds`: `number`
- `fn`: `fun()`
- returns `GearTimer`

#### `gear.every(seconds, fn) -> GearTimer`

Runs `fn` every `seconds`. A timer whose function raised an error stops. At most 1000 timers per mod.

- `seconds`: `number` - Greater than 0.
- `fn`: `fun()`
- returns `GearTimer`

#### `gear.cancel(timer)`

Stops a timer.

- `timer`: `GearTimer`

#### `gear.task(fn)`

Runs `fn` as a task: a coroutine that may wait with `gear.wait` and `gear.wait_until` without holding up the frame. It is resumed every tick (in game every frame; with automation in the menus too).

- `fn`: `fun()`

#### `gear.wait(seconds)`

Inside a task: waits `seconds`.

- `seconds`: `number`

#### `gear.wait_until(test, timeout) -> boolean`

Inside a task: waits until `test()` returns true, at most `timeout` seconds.

- `test`: `fun(): boolean`
- `timeout`: `number` (optional) - Default 30.
- returns `satisfied` `boolean` - True when `test()` returned true, false after the timeout.

#### `gear.guard(where, fn) -> F`

A function that calls `fn` with its arguments and catches its errors: the first error of each `where` is logged with its traceback, later ones are not, and none of them counts against the mod (a mod is switched off after many errors). Use it for handlers that run every frame: `gear.on('draw', gear.guard('draw', draw))`. Returns fn's first result, nil after an error.

- `where`: `string` - A name for the log line, e.g. `'draw'`.
- `fn`: `F`
- returns `F`

#### `gear.log(...)`

A line in `SacredGear.log`, prefixed with the mod's id. Same as `print`.

- `...`: `any`

#### `gear.time() -> number`

Seconds, high resolution, from an arbitrary start.

- returns `number`

#### `gear.read(name) -> string?, string?`

Reads a file of the mod's own folder (directly in it, no subfolders).

- `name`: `string`
- returns `text` `string?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.save(name, text) -> boolean?, string?`

Writes a file in the mod's folder, for settings a mod's own UI changes: `*.json`, `*.txt` or `*.lua` other than `mod.lua` and `main.lua`, at most 8 MB. The write is atomic: the text goes to `<name>.tmp`, is flushed and then replaces the file, so a crash leaves the old file or the new one, never part of one.

- `name`: `string`
- `text`: `string`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

## The manifest (mod.lua)

### GearModManifest

The table `mod.lua` returns. It runs without any globals, so it can only hold values. Annotate it with `---@type GearModManifest` above the `return`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | Required: letters, digits, `_` and `-`; unique among the installed mods. |
| `name` | `string` | Shown in the mod manager and the log (default: the id). (optional) |
| `description` | `string` | One or two lines for the mod manager. (optional) |
| `author` | `string` | Shown in the mod manager. (optional) |
| `version` | `string` | Part of the mod set (default `'0'`). (optional) |
| `priority` | `number` | Lower loads first (default 0); ties load by id. (optional) |
| `requires` | `string[]` | Ids that must load first; the mod is skipped if one is missing. (optional) |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `false`: off until the player switches it on in the mod manager (the default, not a lock). (optional) |
| `settings` | `GearSettingDef[]` | Declared settings: the mod manager builds their page; read them with `gear.settings`. (optional) |
| `keys` | `GearKeyDef[]` | Declared key binds: the player rebinds them in the mod manager; use them with `gear.keys`. (optional) |
| `config` | `table<string, any>` | Default settings: `gear.config` starts as a copy and `config.lua` overrides them. (optional) |
| `pipes` | `string[]` | Names of the named pipes the mod may open (`gear.pipe.open`). (optional) |
| `theme` | `string` | The `.rcss` file (path inside the mod) that Gear puts in front of every RmlUi document of every mod while this mod runs (the shared theme). (optional) |
| `automation` | `boolean` | `true`: the mod gets `gear.auto` when the game runs with `-gear-auto`. (optional) |

## The standard library a mod gets

### GearOs

Reached as `os`.

A mod gets `string`, `table`, `math`, `bit`, `coroutine` and the basic functions below, and from `os` only `clock`, `time`, `date` and `difftime`. Each mod has its own globals.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `clock` | `fun(): number` |  |
| `time` | `fun(t?: table): integer` |  |
| `date` | `fun(format?: string, time?: integer): string\|table` |  |
| `difftime` | `fun(t2: integer, t1: integer): number` |  |

#### `require(name) -> any`

Runs `name.lua` of this mod's folder once (`a.b` is `a\b.lua`) and returns its result (`true` if it returns nothing). Only the mod's own files.

- `name`: `string`
- returns `any`

#### `print(...)`

A line in `SacredGear.log`, prefixed with the mod's id. Same as `gear.log`.

- `...`: `any`

#### `load(chunk, chunkname, mode, env)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `loadstring(text, chunkname)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `loadfile(filename)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `dofile(filename)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `collectgarbage(opt, arg)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `getfenv(f)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `setfenv(f, table)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `newproxy(arg)`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

#### `gcinfo()`

*Not available:* Not available to Sacred Gear mods.

## Data tables (gear.data)

### GearData

Reached as `gear.data`.

The engine's data tables: read only, except the abilities.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `object_types` | `GearObjectTypes` | The type records every object refers to (0x80 bytes; id = index, 1..0x7E5F). |
| `creature_types` | `GearTable` | `Pak\Creature.pak`'s records (0x56 bytes). |
| `abilities` | `GearAbilities` | The ability tables of the exe by id (skills, combat arts, spells), which a mod can change. |
| `regions` | `GearRegions` | The engine's region kill countdowns (the Region Boss quest), which a mod can read and change. |

### GearRecord

Written `record` in the signatures.

One record of a table, read in place. Fields are read by byte offset; nil if out of range.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `index` | `integer` | The record's index. |

#### `record:u8(offset) -> integer?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `record:i8(offset) -> integer?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `record:u16(offset) -> integer?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `record:i16(offset) -> integer?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `record:u32(offset) -> integer?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `record:i32(offset) -> integer?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `record:f32(offset) -> number?`

- `offset`: `integer`
- returns `number?`

#### `record:str(offset, max_length) -> string?`

A zero-terminated string.

- `offset`: `integer`
- `max_length`: `integer` (optional) - Default 64.
- returns `string?`

### GearTable

Written `records` in the signatures.

A read only table of records.

#### `records:count() -> integer`

The number of records (0 if the table is not available).

- returns `integer`

#### `records:stride() -> integer`

The size of a record in bytes (0 if the table is not available).

- returns `integer`

#### `records:get(index) -> GearRecord?`

Record `index`, counted from 0.

- `index`: `integer`
- returns `record` `GearRecord?` - nil if out of range.

### GearObjectTypes

Reached as `gear.data.object_types`.

Includes everything of `GearTable`.

The object types. Besides the table functions it knows the types by name.

#### `gear.data.object_types:name(id) -> string?`

The internal name of type `id` (nil if it has none).

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `string?`

#### `gear.data.object_types:display_name(id) -> string?, string?`

The localized name of type `id`: for an item as the game's tooltip shows it (the first line, colour codes removed; made from a scratch item, nothing is registered or sent), for a creature (kind 3) the game's text for its type (nil for the few creature types the game gives no name text, and for types that are neither; fall back to `name`). The names are cached.

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `name` `string?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.data.object_types:label(id) -> string`

What to show the player for type `id`: `display_name`, else `name`, else `'type <id>'`. Never nil.

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `string`

#### `gear.data.object_types:resolve(spec) -> integer?`

The type id that `spec` stands for: a number that is a type, an internal name (any case), or the localized name of a creature type (any case); nil if it names nothing. For turning names that an older version of a mod saved into ids (see "Names and IDs" in Gear.md).

- `spec`: `integer|string`
- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.data.object_types:kind(id) -> integer?`

The kind (the type record's byte +0x2E) of type `id`.

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.data.object_types:find(name) -> integer?`

The id of the type named `name` (any case; the first type with that name).

- `name`: `string`
- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.data.object_types:search(text, limit) -> GearTypeMatch[]`

The types whose name contains `text` (plain text, any case), ordered by id.

- `text`: `string`
- `limit`: `integer` (optional) - Default 100.
- returns `GearTypeMatch[]`

### GearTypeMatch

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` |  |
| `name` | `string` |  (optional) |
| `kind` | `integer` |  (optional) |

## Abilities (gear.data.abilities)

### GearAbilities

Reached as `gear.data.abilities`.

The exe's two ability tables as one table by id: T1 (the combat arts: ids from 1000, 0x78-byte records) and T2 (the spells: ids from 1, 0x94-byte records). `abilities[id]` is the record of ability `id` (nil if there is none); its fields read and write by name. A field has a name where code that uses it proves what it is, and is `unk_<offset>` (in hex) otherwise. Writes go to the live tables, are checked for type and range, and are undone with `restore` (and when the mod is switched off).

#### `gear.data.abilities:ids() -> integer[]`

The ids of all abilities, ascending.

- returns `integer[]`

#### `gear.data.abilities:fields(id) -> GearAbilityField[]?`

The fields of the table that ability `id` is in, ordered by offset.

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `fields` `GearAbilityField[]?` - nil if there is no such ability.

#### `gear.data.abilities:apply(edits) -> integer?, string[]?`

Writes many fields at once: `{[id] = {field = value, ...}}`. Everything is checked first; if any id, field or value is wrong nothing is written and the problems are returned.

- `edits`: `table<integer, table<string, number>>`
- returns `written` `integer?` - The number of fields written (nil if nothing was).
- returns `problems` `string[]?` - What was wrong.

#### `gear.data.abilities:restore() -> integer`

Undoes this mod's writes to the ability tables.

- returns `restored` `integer` - The number of fields restored.

### GearAbilityField

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `offset` | `integer` | The byte offset in the record. |
| `kind` | `string` | `'u8'`, `'i16'`, `'f32'` ... |

### GearAbility

Written `ability` in the signatures.

One ability record. Reading a field of a table the ability is not in (or an unknown name) gives nil; writing one is an error, as is writing a value that does not fit the field or the `id`. Every byte of a record has a name (reverse engineered, docs/CustomClasses.md "Ability record fields"; the editor's data/ability-fields.json has labels, units and formulas per art); the older `unk_<offset>` names still work. A value at level L is `base + L * per_level` for every `*_base` / `*_per_level` pair. Both tables have `id`, `name_text`, `description_text`, `target_mode`, `regen_*`, `class_mask` and `flags`. T1: `effect_base`, `effect_per_level`, `effect2_*`, `param_a_*`, `param_b_*` (what they mean depends on the art), `approach_distance`. T2: the damage pairs `value0..3_*` (= `damage_physical/fire/magic/poison_*`), `attack_mod_*`, `defense_mod_*`, `res_*_*`, `speed_mod_*`, `param0..2_*` and caps.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `table` | `string` | `'T1'` or `'T2'`. |
| `index` | `integer` | The record's index in its table. |
| `kind` | `string` | `'combat_art'` (T1: ids from 1000) or `'spell'` (T2: ids from 1): what the names in the game's texts say they are. |
| `id` | `integer` | The ability's id (a copy's own id). |
| `base` | `integer` | The id of the ability whose code runs (a copy's base; the game's own abilities: their own id). |
| `name_text` | `integer` | The text id of the name (`gear.text.get`). |
| `description_text` | `integer` | The text id of the description. |
| `target_mode` | `integer` | How the ability is aimed: see `gear.classes.target_modes` (0 free, 1 hostile creature, 2 self or friend, 3 ground position, 4 corpse, 5 self centred). |
| `regen_base` | `number` | The regeneration time in seconds is `regen_base + level * regen_per_level` (T1: f32 at +0x40, T2: whole seconds at +0x3E). |
| `regen_per_level` | `number` |  |
| `effect_base` | `number` | T1: the first effect is `effect_base + level * effect_per_level` (level 1..100). |
| `effect_per_level` | `number` | T1. |
| `effect2_base` | `number` | T1: the second effect. |
| `effect2_per_level` | `number` | T1. |

## Game text (gear.text)

### GearText

Reached as `gear.text`.

The game's own texts, by the text ids its data tables hold (not the keys of `global.res`).

#### `gear.text.get(id) -> string?`

The text for `id` (UTF-8), nil if the game has none.

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `string?`

#### `gear.text.set(id, text) -> boolean?, string?`

Replaces the text of an id the game has (a text is a string or `{en = ..., de = ..., ru = ...}`: the game's language, else `en`, else any). Ids from 0x100000 are Gear's own (`add`). Ids the game does not have are refused.

- `id`: `integer`
- `text`: `string|table<string, string>`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.text.add(text) -> integer?, string?`

Makes a new text of Gear's own and returns its id (from 0x100000), which the game's text lookup serves: for the `name_text` and `description_text` of ability copies.

- `text`: `string|table<string, string>`
- returns `id` `integer?`
- returns `error` `string?`

## Files (gear.files)

### GearFiles

Reached as `gear.files`.

The file overlay: a mod's own data files served where the game opens the original ones, and the mod's own save folder. Declared in `mods/<id>/overlay.txt` (`game\path = data\file` per line, `saves = save`), read when Sacred Gear starts because the game opens its data files before any Lua runs. The rules and the patch formats: [Gear.md](Gear.md#replacing-game-files-file-overlay).

#### `gear.files.overlay() -> GearOverlayInfo?`

What this mod's overlay does, nil if the mod has no `overlay.txt` (or the run does not use it).

- returns `GearOverlayInfo?`

#### `gear.files.resolve(path) -> string`

The path the game's open of `path` (relative to the game folder) ends up at: the mod's file if an overlay rule applies, else `path` unchanged.

- `path`: `string`
- returns `string`

#### `gear.files.served(path) -> integer`

How many times the game opened `path` (relative to the game folder) and was served a mod's file by the overlay.

- `path`: `string`
- returns `integer`

### GearOverlayInfo

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `files` | `integer` | The number of file rules. |
| `saves` | `string` | The mod's save folder (absolute) if the game's `Save\` folder is redirected to it. (optional) |

## Engine hooks (gear.hooks)

### GearHooks

Reached as `gear.hooks`.

The engine hooks that ask mods for a value inside the game's own code (see the events `level.factor`).

#### `gear.hooks.stats(name) -> GearHookStats`

The counters of a hook since the game started: how often the engine asked, how often a mod answered, and how often Lua could not take the question (busy: it was running on this or another thread, so the engine kept its own value).

- `name`: `'level.factor'|'combat.constant'|'creature.ability'|'damage'|'effect.add'|'bonus.constant'|'skillslot.select'|'combat.branch'|'skillslot.key'`
- returns `GearHookStats`

#### `gear.hooks.sites() -> GearHookSite[]`

Every hook site and how often the engine ran it (a site whose function was not found or whose code did not match is listed with address 0).

- returns `GearHookSite[]`

### GearHookSite

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `hook` | `string` | The hook's name (`level.factor`, or the name of a `combat.constant`). |
| `index` | `integer` | The place among those of that name. |
| `address` | `integer` | Where the site is in the game. |
| `calls` | `integer` | How many times the engine ran the site. |

### GearHookStats

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|

#### `gear.pipe.open(name) -> GearPipe`

A client of `\\.\pipe\<name>`; the name must be listed in `pipes` in `mod.lua`. The client reconnects by itself. Messages are framed with a 16-bit little-endian length (the risen-twitch / Gothic Twitch connector's format).

- `name`: `string`
- returns `GearPipe`

Written `pipe` in the signatures.

A pipe client. Set `on_message`, `on_connect` and `on_disconnect` to receive.

| `on_disconnect` | `fun()` | Called when it is lost. (optional) |

### GearRegion

Written `regions` in the signatures.

One region of the kill countdown: when `kills_left` reaches 0 the region boss comes.

### GearRegions

The region kill table. The game keeps its progress in memory only: it is not in savegames, and the game resets it when a region is left.

#### `GearRegions:count() -> integer`

The number of records (32; record 0 is unused), 0 if the table is not available.

- returns `integer`

#### `GearRegions:get(index) -> GearRegion?`

The record `index` (1 .. count - 1).

- `index`: `integer`

The region a sector lies in (a sector word, as `creature:sector()` gives). nil where the game has no region.

- returns `code` `integer?` - The region byte the map files give the sector.

- `creature`: `Creature`

### GearWorld

Reached as `gear.world`.

Positions are world units (`TILE`, about 53.7, is one tile; the screen shows about 534 x 400 around the hero) and a layer (0 outdoors; dungeons have their own). The functions that change the world work only in single player (`can_change()`); in a network game they return nil and a message.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `TILE` | `number` | World units per tile. |
| `CLASSES` | `GearClassInfo[]` | The hero classes. |
| `QUALITIES` | `GearQuality[]` | Item qualities in ascending order; `quality_rank` is the index. |
| `QUALITY_COLORS` | `table<GearQuality, integer>` | The game's item label colours (ARGB) by quality: white, blue, yellow, gold, green for set items. |

#### `gear.world.hero() -> Creature?`

The local hero, or nil.

- returns `Creature?`

#### `gear.world.object(id) -> Creature?`

The object with `id` (as a creature handle), or nil if there is none.

- `id`: `integer`

#### `gear.world.can_change() -> boolean`

Whether the world may be changed now (a single player game runs).

#### `gear.world.open_teleporter(sub) -> boolean?, string?`

Opens the game's list of the portals the local hero knows (the "Transferportal" window), as a portal does: the hero can move to any of its open portals. `sub` is the script command's sub-command, 5 or 6 (both show the list); by default the game's own kind word picks it, as ReBorn's teleportation potion does (6 when the word is 1, which it is in the plain game, else 5). Nothing is charged.

- `sub`: `integer` (optional) - 5, 6 or nil (the game's choice).
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.world.show_text(text_id, color) -> boolean?, string?`

Shows a line of the game's text `text_id` in the HUD, as the game's own refusals ("Enemy is near!") do. `color` is 0xAARRGGBB (the game's refusals use 0xFFFF0000, red; 0 or nil leaves it to the game).

- `text_id`: `integer` - A text id of the game's texts (`gear.text.get`), below 0x80000000.
- `color`: `integer` (optional)
- returns `ok` `boolean?`

#### `gear.world.portals(mask) -> integer?, string?`

The portals the local hero knows (one bit per portal, as the script command Teleporter sets them). With `mask` they are set (single player; the other players are not told).

- `opts`: `GearNearOpts` (optional)
- returns `Creature[]`

The colour of a quality (ARGB, `QUALITY_COLORS`): a quality name, or a rarity 0..15 with `set` for set items.

The colour the game gives an item's name and ground label (ARGB): as `quality_color`, but items for one class take that class's colour unless the game's UNIQUE_COLOR setting is on. Nil when the item is gone.

- `item`: `GearItem|integer` - An item or its id.
- returns `integer?`

A random point between `min` and `max` world units from (x, y).

#### `gear.world.spawn(type, x, y, opts) -> Creature?, string?`

Creates an object of `type` (a type id or an object type name) at (x, y), as the game's own scripts do. Single player only.

- `type`: `integer|string`

An item object as a table, or nil.

Whether `class` can use the item.

- `item`: `GearItem`

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.world.pickup_rules(rules)`

Sets this mod's pickup rules, replacing its previous ones (`nil`: none). The local hero does not pick up the `block` items (a click on them does nothing, the automatic collecting passes them by), and the ground labels of the `dim` items are drawn with their alpha scaled to `dim_alpha`. The rules of all mods are merged after each tick. They hold in single player and for the host's own hero. Item ids are only valid while the item exists.

- `rules`: `GearPickupRules` (optional)

#### `gear.world.pickup_refused() -> integer`

The number of pickups refused so far.

- returns `integer`

### GearNearOpts

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `layer` | `integer` | The layer (default 0). (optional) |
| `limit` | `integer` | At most this many (default 64). (optional) |

### GearSpawnOpts

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `layer` | `integer` | Default: the hero's layer. (optional) |
| `like` | `Creature\|integer` | A creature whose allegiance the new one takes (`creature:copy_allegiance`); if that fails the new creature is removed and spawn fails. A plain create has the faction of its type, which can differ from a creature the game placed (a soldier hostile to the hero by its spawn, neutral by its type). (optional) |
| `label` | `any` | Kept for the creature this session (`creature:label()`). (optional) |
| `modifiers` | `GearModifiers` | Boss modifiers (`creature:set_modifiers`) set on the new creature; if they are refused the creature is removed again and spawn fails. (optional) |

### GearModifiers

Boss modifiers of one creature (`creature:set_modifiers`). A field left out does nothing. The health is written into the creature (maximum and current value); the rest is applied by Gear's `damage` hook on every hit the engine resolves, so it holds for melee, arrows and spells alike as far as they reach the hook. Modifiers exist for this session only: they are forgotten when a savegame is loaded (object ids then mean other creatures). A savegame written while a boss exists keeps it as a plain strong creature (its boosted maximum and current health); to keep the boss, store its id, type and `base_hp` in `gear.store.game` and call `set_modifiers{health = ..., base_hp = ...}` after the load (the world-events mod does). Not available: size, movement speed and resistances other than `taken`. Test: `gear/examples/bosstest`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `health` | `number` | Maximum health as a multiple of the creature's own (0.01 to 100000); the creature starts at full health. (optional) |
| `max_hp` | `integer` | Maximum health as an absolute number (wins over `health`). (optional) |
| `damage` | `number` | Multiplier of the damage the creature deals (0 to 1000; the engine keeps 16 bit: at most 65534 per hit). (optional) |
| `taken` | `number` | Multiplier of the damage the creature takes (0 to 1000; 0.5 is a deflecting armour, 0 immunity). (optional) |
| `deflect` | `number` | Chance 0 to 1 that a hit does no damage at all. (optional) |
| `reflect` | `number` | Fraction (0 to 10) of the damage the creature takes that the attacker takes back. The attacker keeps at least 1 hit point (reflection never kills); nothing is reflected onto the creature itself. (optional) |
| `regen` | `number` | Health regained per second as a fraction of the maximum (0 to 1, e.g. 0.01). (optional) |
| `base_hp` | `integer` | The creature's own maximum health, when `health` is applied to a creature that already holds the boosted maximum: a creature loaded from a savegame that was written while it was a boss. Without it the creature's current maximum counts as its own. (optional) |

### GearModifierStats

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `base_max_hp` | `integer` | The creature's own maximum health before the modifiers. |
| `hits` | `integer` | Hits the creature took. |
| `deflected` | `integer` | Of them, the ones it deflected. |
| `damage` | `integer` | Damage it took (after `taken`). |
| `reflected` | `integer` | Damage reflected onto attackers. |
| `dealt` | `integer` | Hits it dealt with `damage` applied. |
| `max_hp_resets` | `integer` | How often the engine put the creature's own maximum health back and Gear wrote the boss maximum again. |

### GearPickupRules

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `block` | `integer[]` | Item ids the local hero does not pick up. (optional) |
| `dim` | `integer[]` | Item ids whose ground labels are dimmed. (optional) |
| `dim_alpha` | `integer` | Alpha 0..255 for dimmed labels (default 96). (optional) |

Sends the creature the message a drunk potion sends its drinker, so a mod can give a potion its own numbers (the potion handler's effects: 6, 7 and 9 refill health or mana, 8 removes poison by `value` percent, 10 the concentration potions' combo refill).

Gives this creature the allegiance of `source`: its faction (the class the game's hostility table is indexed by) and the aggression flag. A creature made by `gear.world.spawn` has the faction of its type; one the game placed (a sector fill, a script) can have another, so a copy of a hostile soldier may be neutral until this is called. Single player.

- `source`: `Creature|integer`

#### `creature:set_gold(gold) -> boolean?, string?`

Sets the local hero's gold (0 to 2,147,483,646), also in LAN and Open Net games: through the engine's own gold setter, as a merchant sale does, so the hero's next update tells the server and the other players. Other heroes are refused (only their own computer may change them).

#### `creature:set_modifiers(mods) -> boolean?, string?`

Gives the creature boss modifiers (`GearModifiers`: health, damage dealt and taken, deflection, reflection, regeneration), replacing its previous ones; an empty table or nil clears them (the health goes back to the creature's own maximum). Single player only, creatures that are not heroes. Gear reads and writes the maximum health at +0x4D4 and the current at +0x4D8; the effect on hits needs the `damage` hook (installed on demand).

- `mods`: `GearModifiers` (optional)
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

Removes the creature from the world at once, through the engine's own object destroy: no corpse, no loot, no experience. The handle is dead afterwards (`exists()` is false). Heroes are refused. Single player only.

- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

Moves the creature. Single player only.

Takes up the weapons of weapon slot `n` (1-based), as the keys 1-5 do for the hero you play: the old ones go back to their slot. For party heroes (single player).

A hero's experience, the experience its level started at and the experience the next level starts at (the game's own levels), for a gauge: `(now - from) / (to - from)`. Nil for other creatures.

What any creature carries in its equipment slots (0 to 18): monsters, mercenaries and heroes alike. A monster holds the gear that the Disarming skill takes from it there. Nil if the creature is gone.

- returns `{slot: integer, item: GearItem}[]?`

#### `creature:equip_slot(item) -> integer?`

The equipment slot (0..18) an item goes to for this hero, by the engine's own rule: for a group of slots the first one (amulets 6, 7; rings 8 to 11; weapons 12; shields and off-hand items 13), whatever the hero wears. Nil when the hero cannot wear it or it is no equipment.

- `item`: `GearItem|integer` - An item or an item type id.

A hero's combos (the combo master's slots that hold arts), nil for other creatures. Use one with `order_ability(combo.id, target)`.

- returns `GearHeroCombo[]?`

#### `creature:set_combo(slot, arts) -> boolean?, string?`

Writes a combo slot of a party hero as the combo master does: up to four combat arts it knows, at the levels it has them (an empty list clears the slot). Single player.

- `slot`: `integer` - 0 to 3.
- `arts`: `integer[]`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `creature:action() -> GearHeroAction?, integer?, integer?`

What a party hero does now, and the game's raw action and movement states.

- returns `action` `GearHeroAction?`
- returns `action_state` `integer?`
- returns `movement_state` `integer?`

#### `creature:order_move(x, y) -> boolean?, string?`

Orders a party hero (`gear.party`) to walk to (x, y), as a click on the ground does for the controlled one.

- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `creature:order_stop() -> boolean?, string?`

Orders a party hero to stop.

- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `creature:order_attack(target) -> boolean?, string?`

Orders a party hero to attack `target` with its weapon (it walks there first), as a click on an enemy does. In single player (`gear.world.can_change()`) this also works on any other creature, a monster for example: it attacks `target` as a script's order would make it (a creature made by `gear.world.spawn` does not notice heroes on its own, see the spawn-rate mod).

- `target`: `Creature|integer`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `creature:order_ability(ability, target, y) -> boolean?, string?`

Orders a party hero to use a combat art or spell it knows, or one of its combos (`combos()`, ids 0x200 + slot), on a creature (`target`) or a spot (`x`, `y`), as the skill slot does for the controlled one. The game refuses it while the ability regenerates (`ability(id).ready`, `combo.ready`).

- `ability`: `integer`
- `target`: `Creature|integer|number` - A creature, or the x of a spot.
- `y`: `number` (optional) - The y of a spot.
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `creature:learn(ability, level) -> boolean?, string?`

Adds the art (id from 1000) or spell `ability` to a hero's abilities at `level` (default 1), with the game's own function (a rune read does the same). For heroes of the local player and the party (ids 1 to 16). Returns true, or nil and why (`the hero knows it already`).

- `ability`: `integer`
- `level`: `integer` (optional)
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `creature:forget(ability) -> boolean?, string?`

Removes an art or spell from a hero's abilities.

- `ability`: `integer`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `creature:set_name(name) -> boolean?, string?`

Sets the name the game shows for a party hero (1 to 30 characters, UTF-8). The game keeps a companion's name only until the next savegame load: a mod sets it again (the player's own hero keeps the name the savegame has).

- `name`: `string`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `creature:drink_potion(kind) -> boolean?, string?`

Lets a party hero drink a potion from its own backpack, as the potion keys do for the controlled hero (the game picks the potion). Fails if it carries none. The `item.use` event is not asked for this drink (a mod's Lua is running), the potion has the engine's effect.

- `kind`: `'health'|integer` (optional) - `'health'` (default, what Space drinks) or the game's potion kind number.
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `creature:revive(hp) -> boolean?, string?`

Brings a fallen party hero back (`gear.party`). The engine removes a fallen companion from the world (with what it wears and carries) about 25 seconds after it fell, as a network game removes a dead player's hero: revive it before that.

- `hp`: `number` (optional) - Hit points (1 to the maximum; default a quarter of the maximum).
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `creature:add_experience(amount) -> boolean?, string?`

Gives a party hero experience through the game's own gain (it levels up with skill points). Not shared.

- `amount`: `number`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

## Party (gear.party)

Companions are more heroes of the player, at the hero ids 3 to 16, the way a network game holds the players' heroes: each has its own backpack, equipment, attributes, skills, combat arts, spells and experience. The player controls one of them at a time (`control`); the others stand where they are until a mod gives them orders (`creature:order_move`, `order_attack`, `order_ability`). Companions are saved with the savegame like everything in the world. Single player only: in a network game the functions refuse. Loading a savegame gives control back to the hero with id 1.

### GearParty

Reached as `gear.party`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `FIRST_ID` | `integer` | The first companion id (3; id 2 is never used: the engine moves object 2 with the arrow keys in single player). |
| `LAST_ID` | `integer` | The last hero id (16). |

#### `gear.party.available() -> boolean, string?`

Whether the party works now: a single player game with a hero.

- returns `ok` `boolean`
- returns `reason` `string?` - Why not.

#### `gear.party.heroes() -> Creature[]`

The player's heroes in the world, the controlled one first (never another player's hero in a network game).

- returns `Creature[]`

#### `gear.party.mercenaries() -> Creature[]`

The game's own mercenaries that follow the party's heroes (they follow the hero the player controls). The creature orders (`order_move`, `order_attack`, `order_ability`), `abilities`, `action` and `equipment` work for them as for the heroes; their quests and scripts stay the game's.

- returns `Creature[]`

#### `gear.party.leader() -> Creature?`

The hero the player controls (the same as `gear.world.hero()`).

- returns `Creature?`

#### `gear.party.companions() -> Creature[]`

The heroes the player does not control right now.

- returns `Creature[]`

#### `gear.party.recruit(class, opts) -> Creature?, string?`

Creates a companion of `class` where the leader stands (or at `opts.x`, `opts.y`), as the engine creates the player's own hero, with the lowest free id from 3 on. It starts at level 1 without items; `opts.experience` is given through the game's own experience gain, so it levels up with skill points to spend.

- `class`: `GearClassName|integer`
- `opts`: `GearRecruitOpts` (optional)
- returns `companion` `Creature?`
- returns `error` `string?` - `'the party is full'` (ids 3 to 16 taken), or why not.

#### `gear.party.hero_files() -> GearHeroFile[]`

The hero files a companion can come from: the network game's characters (`Save\HeroNN.pax`) and the files `export_hero` wrote into this mod's `heroes` folder. Each file's header is read: call it when a screen opens.

- returns `GearHeroFile[]`

#### `gear.party.recruit_hero(file, opts) -> Creature?, string?`

Brings a hero from a hero file into the party, where the leader stands (or at `opts.x`, `opts.y`): everything it had (level, attributes, skills, combat arts, combos, equipment, backpack) comes along, through the engine's own hero loader. The file stays as it is (the companion is a copy).

- `file`: `string` - `hero_files()[i].file`.
- `opts`: `GearRecruitOpts` (optional)
- returns `companion` `Creature?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.party.export_hero(name) -> string?, string?`

Writes the hero the player controls to `heroes\<name>.pax` in this mod's folder (the network game's hero file format, through the engine's own writer), so another savegame can bring it into its party.

- `name`: `string` - Letters, digits, `_`, `-` (others become `_`), at most 48.
- returns `file` `string?` - The file for `recruit_hero`.
- returns `error` `string?`

### GearHeroFile

A hero file, as `hero_files` lists it.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | `string` | `'save:Hero03.pax'` (the game's Save folder) or `'mod:heroes/<name>.pax'` (this mod's folder). |
| `name` | `string` | The hero's name. |
| `class` | `GearClassName` |  (optional) |
| `class_id` | `integer` |  |
| `level` | `integer` |  |

#### `gear.party.dismiss(companion) -> boolean?, string?`

Removes a companion from the world for good, with what it wears. Refused for the controlled hero and while its backpack holds items (take them first).

- `companion`: `Creature|integer`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.party.control(hero) -> boolean?, string?`

Gives the player control of a party hero: the camera, the HUD, the windows (inventory, skills, combat arts), the mouse, the keys and the controller then serve it, and the hero ids of the game follow (`gear.world.hero()`). The gold goes with control (the party's purse, unless `shared_purse(false)`), and the mercenaries follow the controlled hero. Every mod gets `party.control` `(from, to)` afterwards.

- `hero`: `Creature|integer`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.party.class_portrait(class) -> integer?, string?`

The portrait of a hero class (what `Creature:portrait` returns for a hero of that class), an id for `gear.ui.image`. For a hero file's class in a list. nil if the game has none.

- `class`: `GearClassName|integer`
- returns `image` `integer?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.party.shared_purse(on) -> boolean`

Whether `control` moves the gold to the hero you play (the party's purse, the default). `false`: every hero keeps their own gold (it is in their savegame record as for any hero). Called without an argument it only returns the setting. Not saved: a mod sets it again on every start.

- `on`: `boolean` (optional)
- returns `shared` `boolean`

#### `gear.party.give_gold(from, to, amount) -> boolean?, string?`

Moves gold from one party hero to another (single player): at most what `from` holds and what `to` can take (the game's limit is 2,147,483,646). The hero you play goes through the game's own gold function.

- `from`: `Creature|integer`
- `to`: `Creature|integer`
- `amount`: `number`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.party.share_experience(share, radius)`

Experience a party hero gains from the game (kills, quests) also goes to the other living party heroes within `radius` world units (0 or nil: anywhere), times `share` (1: the same amount, 0: off, the default).

- `share`: `number`
- `radius`: `number` (optional)

| `y` | `number` |  (optional) |
| `layer` | `integer` |  (optional) |

| Value | |

| `'idle'` |  |

## Buffs (gear.buffs)

A buff changes a creature's combat values for a while: its resistances, damage bonuses and factors (armour, attack, speed, regeneration). The game works these values out anew whenever something changes (level, items, its own buffs); Gear adds what the creature's Gear buffs give each time, so they hold through equipment changes and go back when the buff ends or is removed. A buff can also show one of the game's spell overlays on the creature (the stone of Steinhaut, the flames of Flammenhaut, the light of Lichtschild) while it runs. A debuff is a buff with negative values. Definitions are plain data shared by every mod (`definitions` lists them, for editors); a mod applies one to any creature at a strength (0.5: half the values, factors halfway to 1). Buffs are not saved: loading a savegame or starting a new game ends them all (`buff.ended`).

To pass on a buff the game gave (a companion's Steinhaut onto the hero you play): take `fields` of the caster before and after its cast, `change` turns the difference into stats and factors, `apply` them elsewhere.

### GearBuffs

Reached as `gear.buffs`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `STATS` | `table<string, integer>` | The values a buff adds to, by name: `resist_physical`, `resist_fire`, `resist_magic`, `resist_poison`, `damage_min_physical` / `_fire` / `_magic` / `_poison`, `damage_max_physical` / `_fire` / `_magic` / `_poison` (their stats block offsets). |
| `FACTORS` | `table<string, integer>` | The values a buff multiplies, by name: `attack_factor`, `speed_factor`, `armor_factor`, `regen_factor`, `art_regen_factor`. |
| `OVERLAYS` | `table<string, integer>` | The game's spell overlays: `light` (6, Lichtschild), `stone` (7, Steinhaut), `flame` (10, Flammenhaut). |

### GearBuffDef

A buff's definition.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | `'name'` (this mod's: becomes `'mod_id:name'`) or `'other_mod:name'`. |
| `name` | `string` | Shown to the player. (optional) |
| `description` | `string` |  (optional) |
| `icon` | `string` | The game's texture name of its icon (for lists and editors). (optional) |
| `stats` | `table<string\|integer, number>` | What it adds: `{resist_fire = 50}` (names of `STATS`, or stats block offsets). (optional) |
| `factors` | `table<string\|integer, number>` | What it multiplies: `{armor_factor = 1.5}` (names of `FACTORS`, or offsets). (optional) |
| `overlay` | `string\|integer` | The spell overlay shown while it runs: a name of `OVERLAYS` or its number. (optional) |
| `seconds` | `number` | How long it lasts (0 or nil: until removed). (optional) |
| `debuff` | `boolean` | Marks a harmful one (for lists; the values decide what it does). (optional) |

### GearBuffOpts

What `apply` can be told.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `strength` | `number` | 1 (default): as defined; 0.5: half the values and factors halfway to 1. (optional) |
| `seconds` | `number` | Instead of the definition's. (optional) |
| `key` | `string` | One buff per key and creature (default: the definition's id): the same key again replaces it. (optional) |
| `source` | `Creature\|integer` | Who gave it. (optional) |
| `ability` | `integer` | With which combat art or spell. (optional) |
| `overlay` | `integer` | Instead of the definition's. (optional) |

### GearBuff

A running buff (`list`).

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `string` |  |
| `id` | `string` | Its definition's id. |
| `strength` | `number` |  |
| `seconds` | `number` | How long it was given for (0: until removed). |
| `left` | `number` | Seconds left (0 when it has no end). |
| `overlay` | `integer` |  |
| `source` | `Creature` |  (optional) |
| `ability` | `integer` |  (optional) |
| `mods` | `{[1]: integer, [2]: boolean, [3]: number}[]` | What it does: stats block offset, factor (else added), value. |

#### `gear.buffs.define(def) -> GearBuffDef`

Defines (or replaces) a buff. Returns the definition with its full id.

- `def`: `GearBuffDef`
- returns `GearBuffDef`

#### `gear.buffs.definitions() -> GearBuffDef[]`

Every defined buff, in the order they were defined.

- returns `GearBuffDef[]`

#### `gear.buffs.apply(target, buff, opts) -> boolean?, string?`

Gives `target` a buff: a definition's id (`'stone'`, `'other_mod:stone'`) or a definition table (defined on the spot).

- `target`: `Creature|integer`
- `buff`: `string|GearBuffDef`
- `opts`: `GearBuffOpts` (optional)
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.buffs.remove(target, key) -> boolean`

Ends a buff before its time.

- `target`: `Creature|integer`
- `key`: `string`
- returns `found` `boolean`

#### `gear.buffs.list(target) -> GearBuff[]`

The creature's running Gear buffs.

- `target`: `Creature|integer`
- returns `GearBuff[]`

#### `gear.buffs.fields(target) -> table<integer, number>?`

The creature's combat values now, by stats block offset (`{[0x66] = 12.5, ...}`; the offsets of `STATS` and `FACTORS` and more). nil when it is no creature.

- `target`: `Creature|integer`
- returns `table<integer, number>?`

#### `gear.buffs.change(before, after) -> table<integer, number>, table<integer, number>`

What changed between two `fields` snapshots, as `stats` and `factors` of a definition (by offset).

- `before`: `table<integer, number>`
- `after`: `table<integer, number>`
- returns `stats` `table<integer, number>`
- returns `factors` `table<integer, number>`

#### `gear.buffs.overlay(target) -> integer?, number?`

The spell overlay the creature shows and its seconds left (the game's own buffs set it too).

- `target`: `Creature|integer`
- returns `overlay` `integer?`
- returns `seconds` `number?`

#### `gear.buffs.set_overlay(target, which, seconds) -> boolean`

Shows a spell overlay on the creature for `seconds` (default 30; 0 or `which` 0: none). The game counts it down.

- `target`: `Creature|integer`
- `which`: `string|integer`
- `seconds`: `number` (optional)
- returns `ok` `boolean`

#### `creature:buffs() -> GearBuff[]`

The creature's running Gear buffs (`gear.buffs.list`).

- returns `GearBuff[]`

#### `creature:remove_buff(key) -> boolean`

Ends one of its Gear buffs (`gear.buffs.remove`).

- `key`: `string`
- returns `found` `boolean`

## Classes (gear.classes)

A custom class is a profile on top of one of the 8 hero bodies (creature types 1 to 9, `gear.world.CLASSES`): its skills, the arts it can learn (from any class, and monster spells) and the clips it plays. These functions are the engine side of it; the mod `custom-classes` builds the profiles on them. What the engine does, and which arts work on which body (the tiers): [CustomClasses.md](CustomClasses.md). Events: `ability.route`, `motion.select`, `rune.usable`.

### GearClasses

Reached as `gear.classes`.

Hero classes, combat arts and ability copies.

### GearCatalogEntry

One entry of `catalog()`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` | The ability id (combat arts from 1000, spells below; copies: 2000 to 4999). |
| `kind` | `'combat_art'\|'spell'` |  |
| `name` | `string` | The game's name text. (optional) |
| `name_text` | `integer` |  |
| `description_text` | `integer` |  |
| `target_mode` | `integer` | How it is aimed (`gear.data.abilities`). |
| `homes` | `integer[]` | The hero types whose action handlers know the art (empty for spells and monster-only actions). |
| `tiers` | `table<integer, string>` | By hero type: `'home'`, `'A'` (spell: works as is), `'B'` (needs `ability.route` and a motion remap), `'C'` (class state: stays with its class) or `'D'` (no hero handler). |
| `runes` | `integer[]` | Item types of the runes that teach it. |
| `alias` | `integer` | The base ability id, for a copy made by `copy_ability`. (optional) |

#### `gear.classes.catalog() -> GearCatalogEntry[]`

Every ability with its home classes, its portability tier for each body and the runes that teach it.

- returns `GearCatalogEntry[]`

#### `gear.classes.homes(art) -> integer[]`

The hero types (1 to 9) whose action handlers know a combat art.

- `art`: `integer`
- returns `integer[]`

#### `gear.classes.tier(art, body) -> string`

The tier of an ability for a body (`'home'`, `'A'`, `'B'`, `'C'`, `'D'`, see `GearCatalogEntry.tiers`).

- `art`: `integer`
- `body`: `integer|string` - A hero type or its name (`'seraphim'`).
- returns `string`

#### `gear.classes.runes() -> table<integer, integer[]>`

The rune items that teach abilities: `{[ability id] = {item type, ...}}`.

- returns `table<integer, integer[]>`

#### `gear.classes.copy_ability(alias, base, values) -> GearAbility?, string?`

Makes a copy of an ability: a new ability `alias` with its own record (a copy of `base`'s), which `values` change (the field names of `gear.data.abilities`: `effect_base`, `value0_base`, `name_text` ...). Only combat arts can be copied (bases 1000 to 1999), under an id in 2000 to 4999 (the engine refuses art ids above 5000; a copy of a spell was tried and is not run by the engine). The copy runs the base ability's code (its record keeps the base id, which the class handlers switch on); the hero's abilities, the art window, runes and savegames use the copy's id. `gear.text.add` makes texts for `name_text` and `description_text`. The copies are removed when the mod is switched off. `values.spell` (a table of T2 field names) changes the spell record of an art whose numbers live in a spell (see `linked_spell`: Poison Mist 1052 takes damage and duration from spell 12): the copy gets its own copy of that spell record, so the original art and spell keep their numbers. (The handlers push the spell id as a constant: Gear answers that lookup with the alias while the hero has the copy in flight. Tested in a game for Poison Mist; the other spell-linked arts use the same lookup but were not tested.)

- `alias`: `integer`
- `base`: `integer`
- `values`: `table<string, number|table<string, number>>` (optional)
- returns `record` `GearAbility?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.classes.linked_spell(art) -> integer?`

The id of the spell record the game's art `art` takes its numbers from (the engine's map 0x4D1E10: 1018 -> 8, 1019 -> 51, 1044 -> 47, 1049 -> 45, 1050 -> 6, 1051 -> 48, 1052 -> 12, 1053 -> 46), nil for arts that use their own record.

- `art`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.classes.remove_ability(alias) -> boolean`

Removes a copy this mod made.

- `alias`: `integer`
- returns `removed` `boolean`

#### `gear.classes.icon_name(id) -> string?`

The texture file name of an ability's icon (`GUI_MOVE_RUNDUM.TGA`), nil if it has none.

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `string?`

#### `gear.classes.art_icon(id) -> integer?, integer?`

The image id (for `gear.ui.image`) of an ability's icon, the game's own 64 x 64 texture, and the tint to draw it with (the game's icons are grey discs: combat arts gold, spells pale blue); nil if it has none. A copy has its base's icon (give it another with `gear.ui.texture_image(name)` and the record's icon string).

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `image` `integer?`
- returns `color` `integer?`

- `id`: `integer`

Replaces the skill lists in the game's hero record. It is the record of the body, so it applies to every hero of that body (a mod switches it when the controlled hero changes) until `restore_hero_skills`.
