- returns `integer`

## Models (gear.models)

Models.tmp gives every model 256 motion slots, each the index of a motion record (a clip) or 0 for none. The heroes share one biped skeleton, so one body can play another's clip. Changes are for every creature of that model.

### GearModels

Reached as `gear.models`.

The models' motion slot tables.

#### `gear.models.has_motion(body, slot) -> boolean?`

Whether the body's model has a clip for the slot (0 to 255); nil if the model was not found.

- `body`: `integer|string`
- `slot`: `integer`
- returns `boolean?`

#### `gear.models.motion(body, slot) -> integer?`

The motion record the slot maps to (0: none), nil if the model was not found.

- `body`: `integer|string`
- `slot`: `integer`
- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.models.set_motion(body, slot, record) -> boolean`

Maps the slot of the body's model to a motion record (what `motion()` of any body returns), undone by `restore`.

- `body`: `integer|string`
- `slot`: `integer`
- `record`: `integer`
- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.models.restore()`

Puts back the slots `set_motion` changed.

## Drops (gear.drops)

### GearDropRoll

The event table of `drops.roll`: a creature's loot function is about to run. Fields you set are read back; the others are for information.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` | The object id of the source (the dying creature; chests and other sources have ids too), for `gear.world.object(id)` and `creature:carried()`. |
| `creature` | `integer` | The dying creature's type (an index into `gear.data.object_types`). |
| `level` | `integer` | Its level. |
| `forced` | `integer` | The item type of an authored drop (the creature's drop list, a quest item ...), 0 for a random drop. |
| `bonus` | `integer` | The rarity bonus the caller passes (it widens the weights of the rarer qualities; the loot code caps it at 700). Set it to change it. |
| `killer` | `integer` | The killer's object id (a hero: 1 .. 16), 0 when unknown. |
| `survival` | `number` | The caller's survival value (0 for most callers). |
| `network` | `boolean` | True in a network game. |
| `cancel` | `boolean` | Set by the kernel when a handler returned `false`: the roll does not run. (optional) |

### GearDropSelect

The event table of `drops.select`: the loot function asks the equipment type picker for an item. Change `category`, `level` or `quality` to change what the engine picks, or set `type` to use an item type of your own instead of its pick.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `category` | `integer` | The equipment category the loot code chose: 5 weapon, 6 chest armour, 8 ring, 13 shield, 17 helmet, 18 boots, 19 belt, 20 amulet, 21 shoulders, 22 arms, 23 legs, 24 gloves, 25 wings, 29 horse equipment. |
| `level` | `integer` | The level the item is picked for (the creature's level). |
| `quality` | `integer` | The quality (0 plain, 1 .. 14 the rarer tiers; the rarity roll's result as `16 - id`). |
| `hero_pref` | `integer` | The hero type the picker prefers (0 none), for information. |
| `flags` | `integer` | The picker's flags (0, or 2 when the loot code prefers a class), for information. |
| `creature` | `integer` | The dying creature's type. |
| `type` | `integer` | Set it to an item type id (1 .. 0x1FFF) to use that item instead of the engine's pick. (optional) |

### GearRarityRow

A row of the game's rarity table.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` | The table id (2 .. 15 are the qualities 14 .. 1; 0 and 1 hand the roll to the special resource selection; 16 and 17 are plain). |
| `quality` | `integer` | The quality the id gives (`16 - id` for 2 .. 15, 0 otherwise). |
| `kind` | `'quality'\|'special'\|'plain'` | What the row is. |
| `weight` | `integer` | The weight now (after the mods' multipliers). |
| `vanilla` | `integer` | The weight as the game loaded it. |

### GearDropStats

Counters of the drop hooks since the start (or `reset_stats`).

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `rolls` | `integer` | Loot function runs (every creature death with loot, forced or random). |
| `forced` | `integer` | Of them with an authored item type. |
| `vetoed` | `integer` | Rolls a `drops.roll` handler cancelled. |
| `picks` | `integer` | Equipment type picks inside loot rolls. |
| `overridden` | `integer` | Picks a `drops.select` handler replaced with its own type. |
| `rarity_draws` | `integer` | Draws of the rarity roll (1 .. 10000) of all five rarity paths. |
| `rand_calls` | `integer` | Calls of the game's `rand` inside the loot function that the chosen generator answered. |
| `lua_draws` | `integer` | Of them answered by a Lua generator. |
| `quality` | `table<integer, integer>` | Picks by quality 0 .. 15, after the handlers. |
| `category` | `table<integer, integer>` | Picks by category 0 .. 31. |

### GearDrops

Reached as `gear.drops`.

Tuning what creatures drop. Nothing here changes the game until a mod calls it: with no mod the engine's own code runs. The settings of every mod are merged (multipliers multiply; the first mod in load order that chose a generator wins) and applied after each tick, so a setting reaches the next drop. The loot code runs in the host game (a single player game, or the player who owns the creature in a network game); GameServer.exe contains none of it. See `docs/GearDrops.md` for what the engine does and what each setting touches.

#### `gear.drops.chance_scale(multiplier)`

Multiplies the chance of every drop attempt of creatures (the loot code's `budget / 1000` per attempt; above 1000 it runs more passes). `nil` or 1: as the game has it. Authored drops (a creature's drop list) are not affected.

- `multiplier`: `number` (optional) - 0 .. 1000

#### `gear.drops.find_scale(multiplier)`

Multiplies how strongly the rarity bonus ("magic find") widens the weights of the rarer qualities. `nil` or 1: as the game has it.

- `multiplier`: `number` (optional) - 0 .. 1000

#### `gear.drops.rarity_weights(weights)`

Multiplies the weights of the rarity table (replaces this mod's previous multipliers; `nil` clears them). Keys are the qualities 1 .. 14 and `'special0'` / `'special1'`, the two rows that hand the roll to the special resource selection; a key you leave out keeps its weight. The table feeds every path that rolls a rarity (creature loot, containers, the other equipment generators). The roll is 1 .. 10000 against the running sum of the weights (times the level factor and, except for the plain rows, the rarity bonus): the rows are tried in table order (`special0`, `special1`, then quality 14 down to 1, then the plain rows) and the first row whose running sum exceeds the roll wins; a roll that no row catches is plain. So plain items are what is left over and their weights change nothing, and weights that add up to more than 10000 push the later rows (the commoner qualities) out of reach.---@param weights table<integer|string, number>?

#### `gear.drops.rng(spec)`

Chooses the generator of the loot rolls (the chances, the kind of item, the rarity roll): `'fair'` is PCG32 without modulo bias (the game's `rand() % 10000` for the rarity roll favours the first 27.7% of the range by a third), `{seed = n}` the same with a seed (the same rolls every run), a function returns a number in [0, 1) per draw (called a few dozen times per loot roll, keep it cheap), `nil` or `'game'` the game's own.

- `spec`: `'fair'|'game'|{seed: number}|(fun(): number)|nil`

#### `gear.drops.random(n) -> integer`

A number 0 .. n - 1 from the fair generator, for your own rolls.

- `n`: `number`
- returns `integer`

#### `gear.drops.rarity_table() -> GearRarityRow[]`

The game's rarity table now (empty before the first game ran).

- returns `GearRarityRow[]`

#### `gear.drops.stats() -> GearDropStats`

Counters of the drop hooks.

- returns `GearDropStats`

#### `gear.drops.reset_stats()`

Sets the counters to zero.

#### `gear.drops.simulate(creature, count, bonus, forced) -> boolean?, string?`

Makes the engine run the loot function `count` times for a creature (an object id), a few dozen per frame, through all hooks; the items lie in the world afterwards. A tuning and test aid: a single player game only.

- `creature`: `integer`
- `count`: `integer`
- `bonus`: `integer` (optional) - The rarity bonus to roll with (default 0).
- `forced`: `integer` (optional) - An item type id: roll as for an authored drop of that item (default 0: a random drop).
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `message` `string?`

#### `gear.drops.simulation_progress() -> integer, integer`

Rolls done and queued by `simulate`.

- returns `done` `integer`
- returns `queued` `integer`

## Saving (gear.game)

### GearGame

Reached as `gear.game`.

Saving the game through the engine's own save request, the one the savegame window sends: the file is `Save\GAME<slot>.PAK` (slot 0 is the quicksave; the game lists the savegames sorted by file name). Single player only. A save is a request: the engine writes the file a moment later on its render thread, and the result comes as the events `game.saved` and `game.save_failed`. Saves nobody asked this API for (the quicksave key, the savegame window, the game's own Auto-Save) come as `game.saved_other`. Slots 1 to 99 show as `GAME01` to `GAME99`; a mod that saves on its own should keep to slots the player does not use (the game's savegame window picks the first free number for manual saves).

#### `gear.game.difficulty() -> integer?`

The difficulty level of the running game: 0 (bronze) to 4 (niobium); nil if the game is not running.

- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.game.cursor_click(down) -> boolean`

Sends the game's UI a click at the current cursor position, as ReBorn's quick cast does after a skill slot was chosen: the chosen skill is used where the cursor is. False if the UI is not there.

- `down`: `boolean` (optional) - true (default): a mouse button down event, the class ReBorn's cave sends; false: a button up event.
- returns `sent` `boolean`

#### `gear.game.can_save() -> boolean, string?`

Whether a save may start now: a living hero in a single player game, the game itself shown (no cinematic, no window drawn alone, no escape menu or message box), no save or load pending.

- returns `ok` `boolean`
- returns `reason` `string?` - Why not.

### GearSaveOpts

What `save` can be told.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `thumbnail` | `boolean` | Let the engine capture the savegame's picture first (default false: the savegame keeps no new picture). (optional) |
| `window` | `boolean` | Save as the open savegame window's own Save button does, for a mod that replaces the window (`gear.ui.replace_window`): only while that window is open in game; the picture is the one the game took when it opened, and the window closes once the engine took the request. (optional) |

#### `gear.game.save(slot, name, opts) -> boolean?, string?`

Asks the engine to save into slot `slot` (0 to 32766: `Save\GAME05.PAK`, `Save\GAME500.PAK`, ... `Save\GAME32766.PAK`; the game itself stopped at 509). The engine refuses while a trading, chest or similar window is open. Returns true when the request is accepted; the outcome is the event `game.saved` or `game.save_failed`.

- `slot`: `integer`
- `name`: `string` (optional) - The savegame's display name, UTF-8, at most 60 characters; the game keeps Windows-1252 (umlauts and the like), anything else becomes `?`.
- `opts`: `GearSaveOpts` (optional)
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.game.save_pending() -> boolean`

Whether a save (or a load) is queued or being written.

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.game.config(key) -> string|number|nil`

A value of the game's own settings (`Settings.cfg` in the game folder), read only: numbers as numbers (`0` is truthy in Lua, compare it: `gear.game.config('AUTOSAVE') == 1`), everything else as text. The key is not case sensitive. nil if the file has no such key. This is what the game was set to, not a live view: the options window writes the file when the player confirms it, and many settings are read only at start. Useful for warnings about settings that clash with a mod (`AUTOSAVE`: the game's own autosave at script points).

- `key`: `string`
- returns `string|number|nil`

#### `gear.game.config_all() -> table<string, string|number>`

Every value of `Settings.cfg` (see `config`), keyed by the upper case name.

- returns `table<string, string|number>`

### GearSaveInfo

The file of a slot.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `exists` | `boolean` |  |
| `size` | `number` | Bytes. |
| `mtime` | `number` | Last write, unix seconds. |

#### `gear.game.save_info(slot) -> GearSaveInfo?`

The savegame file of `slot`: nil for a slot outside 0..32766, else a table whose `exists` says if the file is there.

- `slot`: `integer`
- returns `GearSaveInfo?`

#### `gear.game.free_slot() -> integer?`

The first slot from 1 up whose savegame file does not exist: the number the game's own *new savegame* picks (its search goes beyond 509 now). nil if every number up to 32766 is taken.

- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.game.reserve_slots(slots)`

Slots this mod writes to itself (the autosave mod's rotation): `free_slot` and the game's own *new savegame* skip them even while their files do not exist yet, so a manual save does not take one a mod is about to use. At most 64 numbers, each 1 to 32766; replaces this mod's earlier list (call it with `{}` to give them back).

- `slots`: `integer[]`

### GearSavegame

Reached as `gear.savegame`.

The savegame being played.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `slot` | `integer` | The number in its file name (`GAME05.PAK`: 5); 0 is the quicksave. |
| `file` | `string` | The file name, e.g. `GAME05.PAK`. |
| `name` | `string` | The savegame's name (UTF-8; may be empty, the game writes `QUICKSAVE` or its "empty" text). |
| `hero` | `string` | The hero's name (UTF-8); nil if the file does not say. (optional) |
| `class` | `GearClassName` | The hero's class; nil if unknown. (optional) |
| `class_id` | `integer` | The hero's class number (1 seraphim .. 9 daemon), 0 if unknown. |
| `level` | `integer` | The hero's level, 0 if unknown. |
| `version` | `integer` | The savegame format (0x1B for Sacred Gold). |
| `compatible` | `boolean` | Whether this game can load it (`version` is 0x1B). |
| `time` | `number` | When it was saved (unix seconds, from the time the game wrote into it); 0 in old savegames. |
| `mtime` | `number` | The file's last write (unix seconds). |
| `size` | `number` | Bytes. |
| `world_date` | `string` | The game world's date and time as the game shows it. |
| `picture` | `boolean` | Whether it has a picture (`save_picture`). |

#### `gear.game.saves() -> GearSavegame[]`

Every savegame in the game's `Save` folder (or the folder a mod's overlay puts it in), sorted by file name like the game's own list. Each file is read for its header: call it when a screen opens, not every frame.

- returns `GearSavegame[]`

#### `gear.game.save_picture(slot) -> integer?`

The savegame's picture (128 x 96, what the game captured when it was saved) as an id for `gear.ui.image`; made on the first call and kept while the file stays the same. nil if it has none.

- `slot`: `integer`
- returns `picture` `integer?`

#### `gear.game.load(slot) -> boolean?, string?`

Loads a savegame, as the savegame window's Load does: in a single player game or from the menus (the open savegame window closes). Refuses a savegame of another version.

#### `gear.game.delete_save(slot) -> boolean?, string?`

Deletes a savegame's file (the game's savegame windows read their lists again).

### GearRealm

An online play (register / login) server the game can talk to.

| Field | Type | |

### GearRealmApi

Reached as `gear.realm`.

Choosing the server of the game's online play (register and login). The game reads the lobby host and port when the multiplayer menu opens Closed or Open Internet (LAN is not touched), so a chosen realm applies from the next time the player opens one of those; an open lobby connection keeps its server until the player leaves. The choice is native (`mods\gear_realm.txt`, applied before any mod loads); the list and the active realm are kept in `mods\gear_realms.json`. A realm names the server the player's password goes to: add realms only from sources you trust.

#### `gear.realm.list() -> GearRealm[]`

- returns `GearRealm[]`

#### `gear.realm.current() -> GearRealm`

The chosen realm.

- returns `GearRealm`

#### `gear.realm.add(def) -> boolean?, string?`

Adds a realm, or replaces the one with that id. `id` is 1 to 32 letters, digits, `_` or `-` and is not `'default'`; `host` is a valid host name or IPv4 address (letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`); `port` 1 to 65535 (omitted: the game's NETWORK_LOBBYPORT).

- `def`: `{id: string, name?: string, host: string, port?: integer}`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `message` `string?` - Why not.

#### `gear.realm.remove(id) -> boolean?, string?`

Removes a realm; not the built-in one and not the one in use.

- `id`: `string`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `message` `string?` - Why not.

#### `gear.realm.use(id) -> boolean?, string?`

Chooses the realm for the next Closed or Open Internet and saves the choice. Raises the event `realm.changed` when the realm changed.

- `id`: `string`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `message` `string?` - Why not.

## Multiplayer (gear.mp)

In a network game every player is a hero object (slots 1 to 16 are the object ids of the heroes). A mod runs on every player's computer; the `kill` event runs on the computer of the player who made the kill. Mods on different computers talk through the mod channel (`gear.mp.send` and the `mp_message` event), which rides the game's own connection. How it works and the messages it builds on: `docs/GearMultiplayer.md`.

The host is the player whose game started the server. In single player the local player is the host and slot 1.

### GearPlayer

A player of the game.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `slot` | `integer` | The player's slot, 1 to 16; the same number as the hero's object id. 0 for the server (`mp_message` only). |
| `name` | `string` | The hero's name as the game shows it (`'hero <slot>'` if the game has none for it). |
| `key` | `string` | An identity for storage: the name in lower case, `:` and the class (`'aria:seraphim'`); opaque, stable between sessions, not unique across computers. |
| `class` | `GearClassName` | The hero's class. (optional) |
| `is_local` | `boolean` | This is the player at this computer. |
| `is_host` | `boolean` | This player is the host (started the game). Always true for the local player in single player. |

#### `GearPlayer:hero() -> Creature`

The player's hero.

- returns `Creature`

### GearMp

Reached as `gear.mp`.

Players of a network game and the mod channel.

#### `gear.mp.players() -> GearPlayer[]`

The players whose heroes are in the game, by slot. Empty before a game runs.

- returns `GearPlayer[]`

#### `gear.mp.player(slot) -> GearPlayer?`

The player in `slot` (1 to 16), or nil.

- `slot`: `integer`
- returns `GearPlayer?`

#### `gear.mp.local_player() -> GearPlayer?`

The player at this computer, or nil.

- returns `GearPlayer?`

#### `gear.mp.active() -> boolean`

Whether the heroes of other players are in the game (a network game with more than the local player).

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.mp.local_slot() -> integer?`

The local player's slot (the local hero's object id); 1 in single player, nil in a network game before the hero is there.

- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.mp.host_slot() -> integer?`

The host's slot; the local slot in single player, nil in a network game while the host is not known yet.

- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.mp.mode() -> 'single'|'lan'|'open'|'closed'`

The kind of game: `'single'` (no network game), `'lan'` (the multiplayer menu's LAN), `'open'` (Open Internet, characters on the players' computers) or `'closed'` (Closed Internet: the heroes belong to lobby accounts and the server keeps them). Default-deny: a game entered through the Internet menu is `'closed'` unless Open Net is proven. Read from the engine, not from anything a mod or the player can set: the net object's bytes ("the Internet menu was used", "lobby identity checked") and the hero's source: in Closed Net the server delivers the hero (message 0x132); in Open Net none comes, so the game reads `'open'` once the hero has been in the game for 10 s with the receive hook in and none arrived. `'lan'` only when entered through the LAN menu. Anything that cannot be read counts as `'closed'`.

- returns `mode` `'single'|'lan'|'open'|'closed'`

#### `gear.mp.is_host() -> boolean`

Whether this computer is the host (always true in single player).

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.mp.send(channel, payload, to) -> boolean?, string?`

Sends `payload` to the mods on another computer (or this one), which get it as the `mp_message` event `(from, channel, payload)`. `channel` names what the message is for (1 to 32 letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `-`; use your mod's id). `payload` is a table (sent as JSON, `gear.json` rules) or a string, at most 64 KB. `to` is a slot, a player, `'host'` (the default) or `'all'` (every player, this one included).

Messages to this computer (single player, or the host sending to itself) arrive on the next tick without the network. Others travel as frames of the game's private chat, which every game server relays; players never see them. Sending is paced (about 8 KB/s), so a 64 KB message takes about 8 s; messages to one player arrive in the order they were sent. Incomplete messages (a player left mid-message) are dropped after 30 s. Nothing is encrypted, and a modified client can send anything: check what you receive.

- `channel`: `string`
- `payload`: `table|string`
- `to`: `integer|GearPlayer|'host'|'all'` (optional)
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?` - `'the host is not known yet'`, `'no such player'`, `'too many messages are waiting to be sent'`, a bad channel or payload ...

#### `gear.mp.force_network(on)`

Debug: `true` sends messages to the local slot through the real chat carrier (out to the server and back) instead of the loopback, in a network game. For self tests of the channel; off by default.

- `on`: `boolean`

### GearKill

What the `kill` event gets.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `victim` | `Creature` | The creature that died (it is retired a moment later; read what you need at once). |
| `type` | `integer` | Its creature type (nil if the object is already gone). (optional) |
| `type_name` | `string` | The internal name of that type (the model name; match on it, do not show it). (optional) |
| `display_name` | `string` | The name to show the player: the localized name of that type, the internal one if there is none. (optional) |
| `killer` | `GearPlayer` | The player who killed it; nil if a creature or something else did. (optional) |
| `award` | `integer` | Experience the killer got. |
| `by_local` | `boolean` | The local hero killed it. |

## Custom net messages (gear.net)

Named channels between the mods of different computers (and the game server's scripts). A channel works everywhere: its messages ride on the chat carrier (private chat frames every server relays, up to 64 KB, about 8 KB/s) and, where the server agrees, on two message types of their own above the game's range (up to 256 KB, faster). The agreement is made on the chat carrier first: a server that supports channels (the Sacred Gear game server, `Sacred.GameServer` of the SacredEngineRemake) is told by the client (a small chat message on entering the game) and sends a query with the two numbers it offers; the client answers over chat, and one HELLO / HELLO_ACK on the agreed types checks the versions and limits. Plain clients are never written to, so they see no frames as chat. Nothing custom is ever sent to a server that did not ask, so the original `GameServer.exe` and servers with opcodes of their own see only chat. Without the agreement (or when it fails) messages to players still go over chat; messages to `'server'` need a server that supports channels (`gear.net.transport('server')` is nil otherwise). `gear.mp.send` uses the custom messages by itself for players that can. `gear.net.transport` says which way a message would travel.

Every message names a channel (`'auction:bid'`); both sides ask for the same name. A channel's id is the FNV-1a hash of its name; two names with the same id are refused when the second is created. Messages for channels this computer has not created are ignored. The server puts the real sender into the message: the `from` a handler gets cannot be forged by the sender. Nothing is encrypted and a modified client can send anything: check what you receive.

The two message types default to 0x1E0 (control) and 0x1E1 (data). A server with custom types of its own announces the data type itself; the control type is set with `gear.net.configure` before the game connects, with the environment variable `GEAR_NETOPS="0x1E0,0x1E1"`, or in the server's `NETOPS_CONTROL` / `NETOPS_DATA`.

### GearNetChannel

A named channel (`gear.net.channel`).

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The channel's name. |
| `id` | `integer` | Its id on the wire (FNV-1a of the name). |

#### `GearNetChannel:on(fn) -> fun(from: GearPlayer, payload: table|string)`

Calls `fn(from, payload)` for every message that arrives on the channel. `from` is the sending player (slot 0 is the server); `payload` is a table if the sender sent one (JSON) and a string of bytes otherwise. An error in `fn` is logged and does not reach the game. Returns `fn`, for `GearNetChannel:off`.

- `fn`: `fun(from: GearPlayer, payload: table|string)`
- returns `fn` `fun(from: GearPlayer, payload: table|string)`

#### `GearNetChannel:off(fn) -> boolean`

Removes a handler added with `GearNetChannel:on`. Returns whether it was there.

- `fn`: `fun(from: GearPlayer, payload: table|string)`
- returns `removed` `boolean`

#### `GearNetChannel:send(payload, to) -> boolean?, string?`

Sends `payload` (a string of bytes, or a table sent as JSON; at most 64 KB over the chat carrier, `gear.net.limits().max_message`, 256 KB by default, over the custom messages) to `to`: `'server'` (the game server's scripts), `'host'` (the default), `'all'` (everybody else) or a slot or player. Each recipient gets it the best way: over the custom messages when this computer and the player can use them (`gear.net.peer_supported`), else over the chat carrier. The pieces leave over the next ticks, paced (64 KB/s custom, about 8 KB/s chat); messages of one sender arrive in order per transport.

- `payload`: `table|string`
- `to`: `integer|GearPlayer|'server'|'host'|'all'` (optional)
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?` - `'the server does not support net channels'`, a bad target, `'too many messages are waiting to be sent'`, a message that is too large ...

#### `GearNetChannel:transport(to) -> 'custom'|'chat'|'mixed'|nil`

Which way a message to `to` would travel now (same `to` as `GearNetChannel:send`): `'custom'`, `'chat'`, `'mixed'` (some players one way, some the other) or nil when it cannot be sent.

- `to`: `integer|GearPlayer|'server'|'host'|'all'` (optional)
- returns `transport` `'custom'|'chat'|'mixed'|nil`

### GearNetCaps

What the `net_caps` event gets.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `supported` | `boolean` | The server supports the custom messages (the handshake is done). |
| `peers` | `integer[]` | The slots of the players that can use them (this computer's slot included). |
| `chat` | `boolean` | The server supports net channels (it queried this client), at least over the chat carrier. |

### GearNetLimits

What `gear.net.limits` returns: the server's announced limits.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `max_fragment` | `integer` | Bytes of one wire message (the library cuts messages to this). |
| `max_message` | `integer` | Largest message. |
| `bytes_per_second` | `integer` | The rate the server accepts from this computer. |
| `in_flight` | `integer` | Messages of one sender the server follows at once. |

### GearNetConfigureOpts

Options of gear.net.configure.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `control` | `integer` | The control message type (default 0x1E0). (optional) |
| `data` | `integer` | The data message type (default 0x1E1). (optional) |

### GearNet

Reached as `gear.net`.

Custom net messages: named channels between mods on different computers and the game server's scripts.

#### `gear.net.channel(name, opts) -> GearNetChannel?, string?`

The channel `name` (1 to 64 printable ASCII characters; use your mod's id as a prefix, `'auction:bid'`). The same name returns the same channel. nil and a message if the name is bad or has the same id as another channel's name. `opts` is reserved.

- `name`: `string`
- `opts`: `table` (optional)
- returns `channel` `GearNetChannel?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.net.supported() -> boolean`

Whether the custom message types are in use with the game server (the chat query, the answer and HELLO / HELLO_ACK are done). False in single player, before the agreement, and on servers without them; channels still work over chat then (see `gear.net.transport`).

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.net.peer_supported(slot) -> boolean`

Whether the player in `slot` (1 to 16) can use them (told by the server; this computer's slot included).

- `slot`: `integer`
- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.net.transport(to) -> 'custom'|'chat'|'mixed'|nil`

Which way a message to `to` would travel now: `'custom'`, `'chat'`, `'mixed'` or nil when it cannot be sent (no such player, `'server'` while the server does not support net channels).

- `to`: `integer|GearPlayer|'server'|'host'|'all'` (optional)
- returns `transport` `'custom'|'chat'|'mixed'|nil`

#### `gear.net.limits() -> GearNetLimits?`

The server's limits, nil while `supported()` is false.

- returns `GearNetLimits?`

#### `gear.net.configure(opts) -> boolean?, string?`

Restricts the two message types (`control`, `data`: above 0x1D5 and below 0x400, different) a server may offer: the client accepts only these numbers and declines others (channels then stay on chat). Without it the offered numbers are accepted. Only before the game connects (nil and a message once the handshake started).

- `opts`: `GearNetConfigureOpts`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

## Chat lines (gear.chat)

Every line the game adds to its message list at the top of the screen goes to the mods too: chat from other players (to everyone, to the team, private), the game server's messages, the game's own notes (a trade declined, a player joined, ...) and the player's own lines. The `chat.line` event gets each one as it comes; `history` keeps the last 200 of the session, also those that came before the mod loaded. For player chat Gear knows who sent it (from the network message the line was made of). A mod that shows the lines itself (a chat window) can keep the game's own lines off the screen with `replace_overlay`; they come back by themselves when it stops calling it. The lines of a window's own list (the trade window, the private conversation window) are passed on too, unless they are the same line the message list just got.

### GearChatKind

| Value | |
|---|---|
| `'global'` | A player's chat to everyone. |
| `'team'` | A player's chat to the team. |
| `'private'` | A private message to this player. |
| `'server'` | A message of the game server. |
| `'own'` | The player's own line, as the game echoes it. |
| `'system'` | The game's own lines (and chat whose sender could not be told). |
| `'notice'` | The game's separate notices (channel 0x10). |

### GearChatRun

A run of a line's text in one colour (the game's `\c` codes switch colours, `\r` goes back).

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` |  |
| `color` | `integer` | ARGB. |

### GearChatLine

One line, as `chat.line` and `history` give it. Shared by every mod: read it, do not change it.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` | Counts up from 1 in the session. |
| `time` | `number` | `gear.time()` when it came. |
| `text` | `string` | As the game got it (UTF-8), with its backslash codes (`\cAARRGGBB` colour, `\r` reset, `\g` image). |
| `plain` | `string` | The text without the codes. |
| `runs` | `GearChatRun[]` | The text in runs of one colour. |
| `color` | `integer` | The line's colour (ARGB): the game's for its channel (white, light blue for private, tomato for the server, green for own lines) unless the line came with one (team chat: yellow). |
| `channel` | `integer` | The game's channel (1 to 4, 0x10 notices). |
| `kind` | `GearChatKind` |  |
| `main` | `boolean` | The game's message list (false: a window's own list). |
| `hidden` | `boolean` | The game did not show it (a mod replaced the overlay). |
| `slot` | `integer` | Player chat: the sender's slot (1 to 16, 0 the server). (optional) |
| `sender` | `string` | Player chat: the sender's name as the game shows it. (optional) |
| `message` | `string` | Player chat: what was written, without the name the game puts before it. (optional) |

### GearChat

Reached as `gear.chat`.

The game's chat and message lines.

#### `gear.chat.available() -> boolean`

Whether the lines can be read (the game's message list was found in this build).

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.chat.history(n) -> GearChatLine[]`

The last `n` lines of the session (all that are kept, up to 200, without `n`), oldest first.

- `n`: `integer` (optional)
- returns `GearChatLine[]`

#### `gear.chat.replace_overlay() -> boolean`

Call it every tick the mod shows the lines itself: the game then adds no line to its own message list (its chat and message lines at the top of the screen stay empty; the lines still reach `chat.line`). The game's lines come back half a second after the last call, so a mod that is switched off, stopped by an error or not drawn gives them back by itself. Several mods may call it. Returns `available()`.

- returns `available` `boolean`

#### `gear.chat.segments(text, color) -> GearChatRun[], string`

A text with the game's backslash codes taken apart: its runs of one colour (`color` where no code says otherwise, default white) and the plain text. Also for item names from `gear.ui.item_tooltip_text`.

- `text`: `string`
- `color`: `integer` (optional)
- returns `runs` `GearChatRun[]`
- returns `plain` `string`

## Settings, key binds and the mod manager

A mod declares its settings and key binds in `mod.lua` (`settings`, `keys`); the player changes them, switches the mod on and off and rebinds keys in the **Mods** screen (F11, or the "Mods" button beside the escape menu), and Sacred Gear keeps everything in `mods\gear_mods.json`. The mod reads its values with `gear.settings`, hears changes as `settings.changed`, and gets declared keys through `gear.keys`. A mod switched off in the screen is unloaded at once: it gets `unload`, then its handlers, timers, tasks, pipes, key binds, pickup rules and open widgets are dropped (what it did to the world stays). Switching it on loads it again with a fresh environment (`load`, and `session.start` when a game runs); mods it requires are switched on with it, and mods that require it are off while it is.

### GearSettingType

| Value | |
|---|---|
| `'bool'` | A checkbox: `true` or `false`. |
| `'number'` | A slider from `min` to `max` in steps of `step` (defaults 0, 100, 1). |
| `'choice'` | A dropdown: one of `choices` (a string or number each, or `{value, label}`). |
| `'text'` | A line of text of at most `max_length` characters (default 120). |
| `'color'` | A color: 0xAARRGGBB (set it from a number, `{r, g, b, a}` or `'#AARRGGBB'`). |

### GearSettingChoice

One entry of a `choice` setting's `choices`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string\|number` | What the setting holds when this entry is picked. |
| `label` | `string` | What the screen shows (default: the value). (optional) |

### GearSettingDef

An entry of `settings` in `mod.lua`. The screen builds its page from these; `gear.settings.get(id)` returns the player's value, else the mod's `config` or `config.lua` value for that id, else `default`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | Letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`; unique in the mod. |
| `type` | `GearSettingType` |  |
| `label` | `string` | Shown in the screen (default: the id). `{ability:N}` shows the game's name of combat art or spell N in its language; a label longer than its column is cut (whole in the tooltip). (optional) |
| `default` | `any` | The default value, of the setting's type (default: false, `min`, the first choice, `''`, opaque white). (optional) |
| `min` | `number` | For `number` (default 0). (optional) |
| `max` | `number` | For `number` (default 100). (optional) |
| `step` | `number` | For `number` (default 1). (optional) |
| `choices` | `(string\|number\|GearSettingChoice)[]` | For `choice`. (optional) |
| `max_length` | `integer` | For `text`. (optional) |
| `section` | `string` | A heading: settings in a row with the same section are shown under it. (optional) |
| `tooltip` | `string` | Shown when the cursor rests on the label. (optional) |
| `note` | `string` | A line of explanation shown above this setting (on a section's first setting: what the section is about). `{ability:N}` as in `label`. (optional) |
| `restart` | `boolean` | The mod only reads it at start: the screen says "after restart" (the mod still gets `settings.changed`). (optional) |

### GearKeyDef

An entry of `keys` in `mod.lua`: a key bind the player can change.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | Letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`; unique in the mod. |
| `label` | `string` | Shown in the screen (default: the id). (optional) |
| `default` | `string` | A key with optional modifiers: `'f8'`, `'ctrl+m'`, `'ctrl+shift+k'`; `''` or nil: unbound. (optional) |
| `section` | `string` | A heading: keys in a row with the same section are shown under it. (optional) |
| `second` | `string` | The id of another key that is this one's second slot: the screen shows both on one row (the other key gets no row of its own). (optional) |

### GearSettings

Reached as `gear.settings`.

This mod's declared settings (`settings` in `mod.lua`) with the player's values. Values are checked against the declaration: a number is clamped and put on the step grid, a choice must be one of the choices.

#### `gear.settings.get(id, fallback) -> boolean|number|string`

The value of a setting. An undeclared UPPER_CASE name is a key of the game's `Settings.cfg` and gives that file's text (see `game`), nil if it has no such key; any other undeclared name is an error. With a `fallback`, an undeclared name (or a nil value) gives the fallback instead.

- `id`: `string`
- `fallback`: `any` (optional)
- returns `boolean|number|string`

#### `gear.settings.game(key) -> string?`

The value of `key` in the game's `Settings.cfg` (`KEY : value` lines) as text, nil if the file has no such key. Read each time, so it is what the file says now.

- `key`: `string`
- returns `string?`

#### `gear.settings.set(id, value) -> boolean?, string?`

Sets a value (kept in `gear_mods.json`); the mod's `settings.changed` handlers run if it changed. Returns true, or nil and a message if the value does not fit the setting.

- `id`: `string`
- `value`: `any`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.settings.is_set(id) -> boolean`

Whether the player has set this setting (else `get` returns the default).

- `id`: `string`
- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.settings.all() -> table<string, boolean|number|string>`

Every setting's value, by id.

- returns `table<string, boolean|number|string>`

#### `gear.settings.reset(id)`

Back to the default: one setting, or all of them.

- `id`: `string` (optional)

#### `gear.settings.migrate(name, fn) -> boolean`

Once per mod and file: reads `name`, an old settings file of the mod's folder (JSON), and calls `fn` with the decoded table, so the mod copies the values into its settings. Returns true if it ran, false if the migration was done before or the file does not exist.

- `name`: `string`
- `fn`: `fun(old: table)`
- returns `ran` `boolean`

### GearKeyHandle

A registered key handler; pass it to `gear.keys.off`. Opaque.

### GearKeys

Reached as `gear.keys`.

This mod's declared key binds (`keys` in `mod.lua`). A bind fires when its key is pressed with exactly its modifiers held, once per press, in game and in automation; not while the Mods screen is open.

#### `gear.keys.on(id, fn) -> GearKeyHandle`

Calls `fn` when the declared key `id` is pressed.

- `id`: `string`
- `fn`: `fun()`
- returns `GearKeyHandle`

#### `gear.keys.off(handle)`

Removes a handler.

- `handle`: `GearKeyHandle`

#### `gear.keys.binding(id) -> string`

The key bound to `id` now: the player's choice or the default, like `'ctrl+m'` (`''`: unbound).

- `id`: `string`
- returns `string`

#### `gear.keys.label(id) -> string`

The key bound to `id` now as text for a window title or hint: `'Ctrl+G'`, `'F3'`, `''` if unbound. It follows the player's rebinding, so a title like `'Loot log (' .. gear.keys.label('panel') .. ')'` stays right.

- `id`: `string`
- returns `string`

#### `gear.keys.set(id, binding) -> boolean?, string?`

Rebinds a key from the mod itself (`''` unbinds, nil restores the default). Returns true, or nil and a message for a text that is not a key.

- `id`: `string`
- `binding`: `string` (optional)
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

### GearModListing

What `gear.mods` tells about an installed mod.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` |  |
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `version` | `string` |  |
| `author` | `string` |  |
| `description` | `string` |  |
| `state` | `'on'\|'off'\|'blocked'\|'pending'\|'error'\|'invalid'` | `blocked`: switched on but a mod it requires is off; `pending`: loads with the next tick; `error`: switched off after 10 errors or its `main.lua` failed. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | Whether the player has it switched on. |
| `loaded` | `boolean` |  |
| `builtin` | `boolean` | The mod manager itself. |
| `reason` | `string` | Why it is blocked, failed or invalid. (optional) |
| `errors` | `integer` |  |
| `requires` | `string[]` |  |
| `has_settings` | `boolean` |  |
| `has_keys` | `boolean` |  |
| `has_page` | `boolean` |  |
| `dir` | `string` | The folder under `mods`. |

### GearMods

Reached as `gear.mods`.

The installed mods and the mod manager.

#### `gear.mods.page(fn)`

Adds a page of this mod's own to its screen in the mod manager (a "More" tab after the generated settings): `fn(x, y, w, h)` draws in that rectangle with the mod's own `gear.ui` and returns the height it used. nil removes it.

- `fn`: `fun(x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number): number` (optional)

### GearModsPageRmlOpts

The options of `GearMods.page_rml`: the load options of an RmlUi document plus two hooks.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | `table` | The data model (as `GearRmlLoadOpts.model`). (optional) |
| `calls` | `table<string, fun(args: string[], doc: GearRmlDoc, event: GearRmlEvent)>` | Functions for `data-event-click` attributes. (optional) |
| `on_change` | `fun(doc: GearRmlDoc, model: table)` | Called after the document changed a value itself. (optional) |
| `theme` | `boolean` | `false`: no theme stylesheet. (optional) |
| `on_load` | `fun(doc: GearRmlDoc)` | Called once when the document exists: keep it, fill the model, add listeners. (optional) |
| `update` | `fun(doc: GearRmlDoc)` | Called every frame the page is shown. (optional) |

#### `gear.mods.page_rml(path, opts)`

The same page as an RmlUi document of the mod: `path` is a file of the mod's own folder, loaded as the mod (the same path rules, events and limits as any RmlUi document it loads). `opts` are the load options (`model`, `calls`, `on_change`, `theme`) plus `on_load(doc)`, called once when the document exists (keep it and fill the model), and `update(doc)`, called every frame the page is shown. The document's element with `id="page"` is put in the rectangle of the "More" tab and sized to it (give it `overflow: auto` if its content can be taller); the host touches nothing else of the document, and it is drawn only while its tab is open, so a mod cannot reach outside its own tab. The pad and the mouse work as in any RmlUi document.

- `path`: `string`
- `opts`: `GearModsPageRmlOpts` (optional)

#### `gear.mods.read(id, relative) -> string?, string?`

A file of an installed mod's folder, read only (`relative` is a path inside it, e.g. `arts/venom.json`).

- `id`: `string`
- `relative`: `string`
- returns `text` `string?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.mods.files(id, folder) -> string[]?, string?`

The names of the files directly in a folder of an installed mod (`''`: the mod's own folder), sorted.

- `id`: `string`
- `folder`: `string` (optional)
- returns `names` `string[]?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.mods.list() -> GearModListing[]`

Every installed mod, sorted by name.

- returns `GearModListing[]`

#### `gear.mods.get(id) -> GearModListing?`

One installed mod, or nil.

- `id`: `string`
- returns `GearModListing?`
