## Remapping the game's keys (gear.input)

The game's keys are fixed: I opens the inventory, 6 selects combat art 1, Space drinks the healing potion. A mod that lets the player choose other keys (or mouse buttons) for those actions gives Sacred Gear rules: "this input is that game key". Sacred Gear applies them to the messages the game reads, before any of its handlers, so the game reacts to the new key as if the player had pressed its own, and never sees the original. A rule without target makes an input do nothing (the original key of an action that was moved elsewhere). Rules apply only while the game has the keyboard: in game, with no message box, escape menu, savegame, options or character screen, and no chat line open; elsewhere every key is the game's own. Inputs are keys (the names of `gear.ui.key_pressed`, with `f13` to `f24` for the extra keys of mice and keyboards) and the mouse buttons `mouse3` (middle), `mouse4` and `mouse5` (the side buttons), alone or with `ctrl+`, `shift+` and `alt+`; the modifiers named must be the only ones held. A modifier alone is a binding too (`alt`), for the keys the game polls. Mouse buttons 1 and 2 and Esc cannot be rebound. The declared keys of `mod.lua` take the same names, so the mod manager's rebinding screen (F11, with the controller's key picker) offers them.

### GearInputRule

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | `string` | The input: `'x'`, `'f13'`, `'mouse4'`, `'shift+z'`. |
| `to` | `string` | The game's key it becomes (a key name without modifiers); not with `block`. `ctrl`, `shift`, `alt`, `add` and `subtract` are keys the game polls (Alt shows names, Ctrl attacks in place, numpad +/- zoom): its poll sees the input held instead, and the input's messages go nowhere. (optional) |
| `release` | `string` | Instead of the others: the game's poll of this polled key (`ctrl`, `shift`, `alt`, `add`, `subtract`) sees it released (its own key of an action moved elsewhere). (optional) |
| `block` | `boolean` | The input does nothing in game (with any modifiers held); the original key of a moved action. (optional) |
| `id` | `string` | Reports the press and release of this input to the handler of `gear.input.on`. (optional) |

### GearInput

Reached as `gear.input`.

#### `gear.input.remap(rules)`

Sets this mod's rules (replacing its earlier ones; `{}` removes them). A rule `{from, to}` for a key the game already has under that name (`{from = '6', to = '6'}`) changes nothing; it marks the key as taken over by the mod, so the mod manager does not warn that the game uses it. An exact rule for an input goes before a `block` rule of the same key.

- `rules`: `GearInputRule[]`

#### `gear.input.on(fn) -> table`

Calls `fn(id, down, repeating)` when the input of one of this mod's rules with an `id` is pressed or released (`repeating`: a held key's auto repeat). The game has the key it was turned into at that time.

- `fn`: `fun(id: string, down: boolean, repeating: boolean)`
- returns `handle` `table`

#### `gear.input.off(handle)`

Removes a handler of `on`.

- `handle`: `table`

#### `gear.input.context() -> boolean, boolean`

Whether the rules apply now, and whether the chat line is open.

- returns `applies` `boolean`
- returns `typing` `boolean`

#### `gear.input.capture_start()`

Rebinding screens: remembers which inputs are down, so `capture` returns the first one pressed after it. Call `gear.ui.capture_keys(true)` as well, so the pressed key does not reach the game.

#### `gear.input.capture() -> string?`

The binding (`'ctrl+mouse4'`) of the first key or mouse button pressed since `capture_start`, or nil.

- returns `string?`

#### `gear.input.normalize(text) -> string?`

The canonical text of a binding (`'Ctrl+Z'` gives `'ctrl+z'`; `''` stays), or nil if it is not one.

- `text`: `string`
- returns `string?`

## Inventories (gear.inv)

The game keeps the hero's backpack, the chest and the shops' stock as grids of cells, "containers" (32 of them). The backpack of the hero with object id n is container n (the local hero in single player: 1), the chest is container 17. An item takes w x h cells; `col` and `row` are its top-left cell, counted from 0. Everything that changes an inventory works in single player (`gear.world.can_change()`) and, in a network game, on the local hero's backpack and the chest (`can_change()` below); the calls go through the game's own inventory and object code, so the cells, the items' owners and the object lists stay as when the player moves an item. `export` copies an item to bytes (its type and own data: the random properties), `add` makes it again, so that an item can leave the game and come back unchanged (see the `shared-stash` mod).

### GearContainer

Written `container` in the signatures.

One inventory grid, from `gear.inv.container`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `index` | `integer` | The container's number (0..31). |
| `columns` | `integer` | Cells across. |
| `rows` | `integer` | Cells down. |

#### `container:items() -> GearInvItem[]`

The items in the container, in cell order: `gear.world.item` tables plus the cell and size.

- returns `GearInvItem[]`

#### `container:free_spot(w, h) -> integer?, integer?`

Room for a `w` x `h` item: its top-left cell, or nil.

- `w`: `integer`
- `h`: `integer`
- returns `col` `integer?`
- returns `row` `integer?`

#### `container:put(item_id, col, row) -> boolean?, string?`

Puts an item that lies in the world or was taken out of a container at the cell (the cells must be free).

- `item_id`: `integer`
- `col`: `integer`
- `row`: `integer`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `container:take(item_id) -> boolean?, string?`

Takes the item out; the item object stays (put it somewhere or `gear.inv.destroy` it).

- `item_id`: `integer`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

### GearInvItem

Includes everything of `GearItem`.

An item in a container: a `GearItem` with its place in the grid.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `col` | `integer` | Top-left cell (from 0). |
| `row` | `integer` |  |
| `w` | `integer` | Width in cells. |
| `h` | `integer` | Height in cells. |

### GearInv

Reached as `gear.inv`.

Inventories: containers, the items in them, and items copied to bytes and made again.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `CHEST` | `integer` | The chest's container number (17). |

#### `gear.inv.container(which) -> GearContainer?`

A container: `'chest'`, `'backpack'` (the local hero's) or its number (0..31). Nil if there is none.

- `which`: `'chest'|'backpack'|integer`
- returns `GearContainer?`

#### `gear.inv.can_change() -> boolean, boolean`

Whether the local hero's inventory may be changed now, and whether a network game runs. Single player: as `gear.world.can_change()`. In a network game (LAN, open net) the changes go through the engine's own announcing calls (an item made is announced as created and updated, put in and taken out as inventory moves, destroyed as a destruction) and only the hero's own backpack and the chest may be changed there; spawning stays refused. The temporary items of icons and tooltips are made local-only there: not announced, put in and taken out without the announcing flag and destroyed through the engine's local path.

- returns `allowed` `boolean`
- returns `network` `boolean`

#### `gear.inv.size(item_id) -> integer?, integer?`

The size of an item in cells, or nil.

- `item_id`: `integer`
- returns `w` `integer?`
- returns `h` `integer?`

#### `gear.inv.socket(item_id, upgrade_id) -> boolean?, string?`

Puts an upgrade item (a rune lying in the world, e.g. made with `create`, or in no container) into a free socket of an item, as the blacksmith does: the item gains the rune's bonuses and an entry, the rune is consumed. Single player only.

- `item_id`: `integer`
- `upgrade_id`: `integer`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.inv.export(item_id) -> string?, string?`

Copies an item to a binary string: its type and its own data, not where it is. `hex` makes it text for JSON.

- `item_id`: `integer`
- returns `bytes` `string?`
- returns `error` `string?`

### GearItemRequirements

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `level` | `integer` |  |
| `strength` | `integer` |  |
| `dexterity` | `integer` |  |
| `charisma` | `integer` |  |
| `endurance` | `integer` |  |
| `skill` | `integer` | The required skill's number (0: none). |
| `skill_level` | `integer` |  |

### GearItemBonus

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `slot` | `integer` | 0..7, the bonus slot in its record (what `GearInv.bonus_text` takes). |
| `entry` | `integer` | 0 for the item's own record, 1..n for a merged record (see `GearItemValues.entries`). |
| `code` | `integer` | The bonus's number: 801..808 elemental damage / resistance, 809 attack, 810 defense, 600..798 a skill, 811..868 the named bonuses (`global.res` texts), 1..~140 a combat art, 0x321..0x364 protection groups. |
| `attribute` | `integer` | The hero attribute the stored value is scaled by (1 strength, 2 dexterity, 3 charisma, 4 endurance ... 0: not scaled). |
| `flags` | `integer` | The bonus's type word (low byte: the target kind, bits 8..11 the attribute / element selector, 0x2000 spells only, 0x4000 weapon damage only, 0x8000 resistance for codes 801..808). |
| `value` | `integer` | The stored value (percent or points, by the bonus), as the record keeps it. |

### GearItemRecord

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `integer` | The object type the record was made for. |
| `flags` | `integer` | Raw flags (class bits among them). |
| `price` | `integer` |  |
| `level` | `integer` | The item's level. |
| `requirements` | `GearItemRequirements` |  |
| `attack` | `integer` |  |
| `defense` | `integer` |  |
| `bw` | `integer` |  |
| `protection` | `{physical: integer, fire: integer, magic: integer, poison: integer}` |  |
| `damage` | `{min: integer[], max: integer[]}` | Four values each (the four damage kinds), as stored. |
| `sockets` | `integer[]` | Eight socket kinds (0 none, 1..4 sockets that hold a rune or gem). |
| `bonuses` | `GearItemBonus[]` | The record's own bonus slots that are in use. |
| `blacksmith_level` | `integer` |  |

### GearItemSocketRecord

Includes everything of `GearItemRecord`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `entry` | `integer` | 1..n, the order of `export`. |
| `active` | `boolean` | The engine merges this record into the item (its socket kind is 1..4). |

### GearItemValues

Includes everything of `GearItemRecord`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` | The item's id when read by id. (optional) |
| `entries` | `GearItemSocketRecord[]` | The merged records of the item's sockets and random properties. |

#### `gear.inv.values(item) -> GearItemValues?, string?`

The item's resolved value record decoded (`export`'s block: level, requirements, damage, attack / defense / protection, the eight bonus slots) with the records its sockets merged into it. The numbers are as stored, which is what the game derives its tooltip lines from: bonuses scaled by a hero attribute show the stored percentage times the hero's attribute (use `bonus_text` for the game's own line). Pass an item id or `export`'s bytes.

- `item`: `integer|string`
- returns `values` `GearItemValues?`
- returns `message` `string?`

#### `gear.inv.bonus_text(item_id, entry, slot) -> string?`

The game's own tooltip line of one bonus: slot 0..7 of the item's own record (`entry` 0) or of one of its merged records (1..n), UTF-8 with the game's colour codes, in the game's language, as the tooltip builds it (the controlled hero's attributes included). nil when the item or entry does not exist; empty when the slot has no bonus.

- `item_id`: `integer`
- `entry`: `integer` (optional) - Default 0.
- `slot`: `integer` (optional) - Default 0.
- returns `string?`

#### `gear.inv.create(bytes) -> integer?, string?`

Makes a new item from `export`'s bytes, lying at the hero's feet (single player only). Put it into a container or `destroy` it.

- `bytes`: `string`
- returns `item_id` `integer?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.inv.destroy(item_id) -> boolean?, string?`

Deletes an item that is in no container.

- `item_id`: `integer`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.inv.add(container, bytes) -> integer?, integer|string?, integer?`

Makes a new item from `export`'s bytes straight into the container (the first spot with room). Nothing changes when it fails.

- `container`: `GearContainer`
- `bytes`: `string`
- returns `item_id` `integer?`
- returns `col` `integer|string?` - The cell, or the error message when `item_id` is nil.
- returns `row` `integer?`

#### `gear.inv.remove(container, item_id) -> string?, string?`

Takes the item out of the container, destroys it and returns its export. If that fails the item is where it was.

- `container`: `GearContainer`
- `item_id`: `integer`
- returns `bytes` `string?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.inv.hex(bytes) -> string`

Bytes as lowercase hex text.

- `bytes`: `string`
- returns `string`

#### `gear.inv.unhex(text) -> string?`

Hex text back to bytes, or nil if it is not hex.

- `text`: `string`
- returns `string?`

## Lookups (gear.lookup)

A lookup finds one "thing" in a list of things of one kind: equipment items (named as the game's tooltip names them, in the player's language), creatures, abilities, or a kind a mod registers. The search is forgiving: several words in any order, no matter the case or the accents (`flugel` finds Flügel), one typo is forgiven (`scwert` finds Schwert), a word may be a beginning, and the best matches come first. `search` returns the things; `open` shows a small window where the player types and picks, and a callback gets the thing that was chosen and answers what the lookup returns (`pick` waits for that inside a task). The library is shipped in the DLL (`gear/lua/lookup.lua`) and runs once per mod.

### GearLookupItem

A thing of the built-in kind `'item'`: an equipment item type.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` | The object type id. |
| `name` | `string` | The name the game's tooltip shows (the player's language). |
| `internal` | `string` | The internal type name. |
| `kind` | `integer` | The type record's kind (the equipment class). |

### GearLookupCreature

A thing of the built-in kind `'creature'`: a word of monster type names.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `word` | `string` | Lower case, e.g. `'orc'` (a whole word of names like `ORC_WARRIOR.GRN`). |
| `name` | `string` | The word with a capital. |
| `count` | `integer` | How many monster types carry it. |
| `types` | `integer[]` | Their type ids. |
| `names` | `string[]` | The localized names of those types (the player's language, no duplicates), which the search matches as well. |

### GearLookupCreatureType

A thing of the built-in kind `'creature_type'`: one monster type.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` | The type id (save this). |
| `name` | `string` | The localized name (the internal one if the game has no text for it). |
| `internal` | `string` | The internal name (the model name). |

### GearLookupAbility

A thing of the built-in kind `'ability'`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` |  |
| `name` | `string` | The name in the game's texts. |
| `kind` | `string` | `'combat_art'` or `'spell'`. |

### GearLookupKind

What a mod gives `register`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `things` | `fun(): table[]` | Returns the list of things (called once; `refresh` asks again). Each thing is a table. |
| `label` | `string` | What the picker's title says. (optional) |
| `name` | `fun(thing: table): string` | The name to show (default `thing.name`). (optional) |
| `text` | `fun(thing: table): string` | The text that is searched (default the shown name). (optional) |
| `detail` | `fun(thing: table): string` | A short note after the name in the picker. (optional) |

### GearLookupOpts

The options of `open` and `pick`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` | The window's title. (optional) |
| `text` | `string` | The text the search starts with. (optional) |
| `filter` | `fun(thing: table): boolean` | Return false to leave a thing out. (optional) |
| `select` | `fun(thing: table): any` | Called with the chosen thing; what it returns is the result of the lookup (nil: the thing itself; false: refused, the picker stays open). (optional) |
| `done` | `fun(result: any, thing: table)` | Called with that result. (optional) |
| `multi` | `boolean` | Keep the picker open after a choice, for adding several things; the Done button closes it. (optional) |
| `closed` | `fun(cancelled: boolean)` | Called when the picker is gone. (optional) |

### GearLookup

Reached as `gear.lookup`.

Finding things of the game by name.

#### `gear.lookup.register(kind, def)`

Adds or replaces a kind of things to look up.

- `kind`: `string`
- `def`: `GearLookupKind`

#### `gear.lookup.kinds() -> string[]`

The names of the kinds: `'ability'`, `'creature'`, `'creature_type'`, `'item'` and the registered ones.

- returns `string[]`

#### `gear.lookup.refresh(kind)`

Forgets the list of things of `kind` so that `things` is asked again.

- `kind`: `string`

#### `gear.lookup.search(kind, text, limit, filter) -> table[]`

The things of `kind` that match `text`, best first. An empty text gives the first things in their own order.

- `kind`: `string`
- `text`: `string`
- `limit`: `integer` (optional) - Default 50.
- `filter`: `fun(thing: table): boolean` (optional)
- returns `things` `table[]`

#### `gear.lookup.name(kind, thing) -> string`

The name shown for a thing of `kind`.

- `kind`: `string`
- `thing`: `table`
- returns `string`

#### `gear.lookup.words(text) -> string[]`

The lower case, accent-free words of a text (ä = a, ß = ss), the unit of the matching.

- `text`: `string`
- returns `string[]`

#### `gear.lookup.score(query, words) -> number?`

How well the words of a text match a query (a text or the list `words` makes): higher is better, nil when a query word finds nothing.

- `query`: `string|string[]`
- `words`: `string[]`
- returns `score` `number?`

#### `gear.lookup.open(kind, opts)`

Shows the picker for a kind. The player types, uses the list (mouse, Up and Down, Enter, or the controller's D-pad) and the callbacks of `opts` hear the choice. One picker is open at a time; a new one replaces it.

- `kind`: `string`
- `opts`: `GearLookupOpts` (optional)

#### `gear.lookup.is_open() -> boolean`

Whether the picker is open.

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.lookup.close()`

Closes the picker (`closed(true)` is called).

#### `gear.lookup.pick(kind, opts) -> any`

Inside a task (`gear.task`): opens the picker and waits. Returns what `select` returned (the thing if there is no `select`), nil when the player cancelled.

- `kind`: `string`
- `opts`: `GearLookupOpts` (optional)
- returns `result` `any`

#### `gear.lookup.text_field(id, x, y, w, text, opts) -> string, boolean`

A one-line text field for a mod's own window: draws it, takes the keys while it has the focus (the keyboard only) and returns the new text; the second result is true in the frame Enter was pressed.

- `id`: `string`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `text`: `string`
- `opts`: `{tooltip?: string, max?: integer, focus?: boolean}` (optional)
- returns `text` `string`
- returns `entered` `boolean`

#### `gear.lookup.focused() -> string?`

The id of the text field that has the focus, nil if none.

- returns `string?`

#### `gear.lookup.unfocus()`

Takes the focus away from the text field.

## Formatting (gear.fmt)

Small helpers that many mods need for their panels: a number with thousands separators, seconds as a clock or in words, a text from outside cut to a length (by characters or by its width on screen), the game's colour and image markup taken out of a line. The library is shipped in the DLL (`gear/lua/fmt.lua`) and runs once per mod, the first time the mod uses `gear.fmt`.

### GearFmt

Reached as `gear.fmt`.

Numbers, times and texts made ready to show.

#### `gear.fmt.number(n, sep) -> string`

A whole number with thousands separators: `1234567` -> `'1,234,567'` (rounded; nil and non-numbers count as 0).

- `n`: `number`
- `sep`: `string` (optional) - The separator (default `','`).
- returns `string`

#### `gear.fmt.duration(seconds) -> string`

Seconds as a clock with hours: `3725` -> `'1:02:05'`.

- `seconds`: `number`
- returns `string`

#### `gear.fmt.clock(seconds) -> string`

Seconds as minutes and seconds: `125` -> `'2:05'` (the minutes grow past 59).

- `seconds`: `number`
- returns `string`

#### `gear.fmt.span(seconds) -> string`

Seconds in the two biggest units: `'2d 03h'`, `'1h 02m'`, `'3m 05s'`, `'12s'`.

- `seconds`: `number`
- returns `string`

#### `gear.fmt.fit(text, max) -> string`

A text for one line: nil becomes `''`, control characters become spaces, and a text longer than `max` bytes is cut with `'...'` (never inside a UTF-8 character). Use it for texts that come from a server or another player.

- `text`: `any`
- `max`: `integer` (optional) - Without it the text is not cut.
- returns `string`

#### `gear.fmt.fit_width(text, width, size) -> string`

`text` cut with `'...'` so that it is at most `width` wide in the font of `size` (measured with `gear.ui.text_size`, cached).

- `text`: `string`
- `width`: `number`
- `size`: `number` (optional) - Default 12.
- returns `string`

#### `gear.fmt.plain(line, keep_unknown) -> string?`

A line without the game's text markup (`\cAARRGGBB` colours, `\g...` inline images, `\r`, `\w`) and without leading and trailing spaces. nil when nothing is left, and when other backslash codes remain (unless `keep_unknown`).

- `line`: `string`
- `keep_unknown`: `boolean` (optional)
- returns `string?`

#### `gear.fmt.count(n, one, many) -> string`

A number and a noun: `(1, 'kill')` -> `'1 kill'`, `(3, 'kill')` -> `'3 kills'`.

- `n`: `number`
- `one`: `string`
- `many`: `string` (optional) - Default `one .. 's'`.
- returns `string`

## Toasts (gear.toast)

A toast is a short message (a title and a few lines) that shows at the top of the screen, stacks under the ones before it and fades after a few seconds: an unlocked achievement, a finished bounty. The stack is a bare panel of the mod (`'toasts'`, layout key `<mod id>:toasts`): the layout editor moves it, and shows a sample while it is on; the mouse and the controller go on to the game. A toast's age counts in-game frames. The library is shipped in the DLL (`gear/lua/toast.lua`) and runs once per mod, the first time the mod uses `gear.toast`.

### GearToastSpec

A toast given as a table to `show`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` |  |
| `lines` | `string[]` |  (optional) |
| `color` | `integer` | The accent bar's colour (0xAARRGGBB). (optional) |

### GearToastOpts

The options of `options`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `seconds` | `number\|fun(): number` | How long a toast stays (default 6); a function is asked every frame (e.g. a setting). (optional) |
| `max` | `integer` | How many toasts at once (default 4); the oldest goes first. (optional) |
| `width` | `number` | The width of a toast in layout units (default 360). (optional) |
| `when` | `fun(state: GearUiState): boolean` | Whether toasts are drawn now (default: `state.mode == 'game'`). (optional) |

### GearToast

Reached as `gear.toast`.

This mod's toasts.

#### `gear.toast.show(title, ...)`

Shows a toast: a title and lines (nil and `''` are left out), or a `GearToastSpec`.

- `title`: `string|GearToastSpec`
- `...`: `string` (optional)

#### `gear.toast.options(opts)`

Changes this mod's toast options (each one is kept until changed).

- `opts`: `GearToastOpts`

#### `gear.toast.clear()`

Removes this mod's toasts.

#### `gear.toast.count() -> integer`

How many of this mod's toasts are on the screen.

- returns `integer`

## Stored data (gear.store)

A mod keeps its own data (a log, totals, saved lists) in JSON files of its folder (`gear.read` / `gear.save`). `load` and `save` do the reading, decoding, encoding and writing with defaults and one log line per broken file; `file` loads a table once and saves it when it changed, every few seconds and when the mod unloads. The library is shipped in the DLL (`gear/lua/store.lua`) and runs once per mod, the first time the mod uses `gear.store`.

What belongs to one character or savegame (progress, lifetime totals, a log) goes in `gear.store.game` instead of `file`: it is kept per savegame (see `gear.savegame`), so it does not leak from one savegame or character into another. Settings, window places and what all games share stay in `file` / `load` / `save`.

### GearStoreOpts

The options of `file`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `every` | `number` | Seconds between saves of a changed file (default 30; 0: only on unload and `save`). (optional) |
| `check` | `fun(data: any): any` | Repairs or replaces what was loaded (called once). (optional) |
| `value` | `fun(): any` | What is written (default `handle.data`). (optional) |

### GearStoreGameOpts

Includes everything of `GearStoreOpts`.

The options of `game` (those of `file`, and):

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `on_change` | `fun(handle: GearStoreFile, kind: 'load'\|'hero'\|'new', scope: string?)` | Called after the handle holds the data of another game (the mod's `savegame.changed` handlers run after it). (optional) |
| `migrate` | `boolean` | A file `name` of the mod's folder from before the mod used per game data is taken once, by the first loaded savegame that has no data yet; `<name>.migrated.txt` records it. (optional) |

### GearStoreFile

A file of `gear.store.file`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `data` | `any` | The loaded table (or the default); change it, then call `changed`. |
| `dirty` | `boolean` |  |

#### `GearStoreFile:changed()`

Marks the data as changed: it is written at the next save.

#### `GearStoreFile:save() -> boolean, string?`

Writes the file now.

- returns `ok` `boolean`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `GearStoreFile:flush() -> boolean, string?`

Writes the file if it changed.

- returns `ok` `boolean`
- returns `error` `string?`

### GearStore

Reached as `gear.store`.

JSON files of the mod's folder.

#### `gear.store.load(name, default) -> T, ('missing'|'invalid')?`

The decoded file, or `default` when it is missing, not JSON, or not a table while `default` is one. The second result is `'missing'` or `'invalid'` when the default was taken.

- `name`: `string`
- `default`: `T`
- returns `data` `T`
- returns `why` `('missing'|'invalid')?`

#### `gear.store.save(name, value) -> boolean, string?`

Writes `value` as JSON. The first failure of each file is logged.

- `name`: `string`
- `value`: `any`
- returns `ok` `boolean`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.store.file(name, default, opts) -> GearStoreFile`

Loads `name` (or takes `default`) and keeps it: the handle saves it when it changed (see `GearStoreOpts`) and on unload.

- `name`: `string`
- `default`: `any`
- `opts`: `GearStoreOpts` (optional)
- returns `GearStoreFile`

#### `gear.store.game(name, default, opts) -> GearStoreFile`

A file of the savegame being played: what the mod keeps about this character or game. The same handle as `file`, but the data belongs to the savegame: saving the game into a slot keeps it for that slot, loading a slot brings back what was kept for it (the defaults if nothing was), a new game starts from `default`. Progress made since the last save is dropped when another game loads, as the game's own progress is, and `handle.data` is replaced then: always reach the data through the handle (`handle.data.x`), never keep a part of it. Files are in `saves/<scope>/` of the mod's folder.

- `name`: `string`
- `default`: `any`
- `opts`: `GearStoreGameOpts` (optional)
- returns `GearStoreFile`

## Per savegame data (gear.savegame)

Mods keep two kinds of data: what is the player's (settings, window places, a stash all characters share) and what belongs to one character or game (progress, lifetime totals, a log). The second kind must not leak from one savegame into another, so Gear keeps a working copy of it per mod in `saves/_current/` of the mod's folder and moves it with the game:

- a save (the savegame window, the quicksave, the game's own auto save, `gear.game.save`) keeps the working copy for that savegame, in `saves/GAME05/` for `Save\GAME05.PAK` (first the event `savegame.saving`, so a mod can write what changed); - loading a savegame (from the menus, the savegame window, `gear.game.load`) replaces the working copy with the one kept for it, or empties it if there is none (then the mod starts from its defaults); a network game's hero file (`Save\Hero03.pax`) has the scope `HERO03` and is kept when the game writes it; - a new game empties the working copy; deleting a savegame (`gear.game.delete_save`) deletes what was kept for it.

Before that, `savegame.leaving` `(scope, kind)` lets a mod write into the data kept for the game that ends. After a load or a new game the event `savegame.changed` `(kind, scope, number)` tells the mods to read their data again; progress since the last save is gone, as the game's own is. The scope is the file's name (`GAME05`); when the game reads its savegames from another folder than `Save` (ReBorn: `mods\reborn\save`) it has the folder in front: `mods_reborn_save-GAME05`.

Most mods use `gear.store.game` (a JSON file with the usual handle) and never touch this API directly. Not for settings (use `gear.settings`) and not for what all savegames share (use `gear.store.file`).

Known limits: the load and new game commands are seen where the game runs them; a savegame copied or deleted outside the game keeps (or loses) nothing here; in a network game the data follows the hero file, not the server.

#### `gear.savegame.scope() -> string?`

The savegame this game was loaded from or last saved to: `'GAME05'` (`Save\GAME05.PAK`), `'HERO03'` (a network hero file), `<folder>-GAME05` when the game reads its savegames from another folder. nil in a new game that was not saved yet.

- returns `string?`

#### `gear.savegame.kind() -> ('load'|'hero'|'new')?`

How this game started: `'load'` (a savegame), `'hero'` (a network hero file), `'new'` (a new game); nil if the game's load command was not seen (the game was running before Gear, or the command was not found: the data is then global as before).

- returns `('load'|'hero'|'new')?`

#### `gear.savegame.scope_of(slot) -> string`

The scope name of savegame `slot` (`'GAME05'`).

- `slot`: `integer`
- returns `string`

#### `gear.savegame.read(name) -> string?, string?`

A file of this mod's data of the running game (`.json` or `.txt`, a name of letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`). Using this API makes Gear keep the mod's data per savegame.

- `name`: `string`
- returns `text` `string?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.savegame.write(name, text) -> boolean?, string?`

Writes a file of this mod's data of the running game (atomic, at most 8 MB).

- `name`: `string`
- `text`: `string`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.savegame.write_saved(scope, name, text) -> boolean?, string?`

Writes a file of the data kept for savegame `scope` (not the running game's own). For what a mod learns after the savegame was written and must attribute to it, such as the time played when the game ends: write it in the handler of `savegame.leaving`.

- `scope`: `string`
- `name`: `string`
- `text`: `string`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.savegame.read_saved(scope, name) -> string?, string?`

A file of the data kept for another savegame (for a list that shows what each savegame holds).

- `scope`: `string`
- `name`: `string`
- returns `text` `string?`
- returns `error` `string?`

## Hooks between mods (gear.events)

A mod that has something other mods may want to react to (a bounty that is done, a world event that starts) *publishes a hook*: it declares a custom event with `gear.events.declare` and fires it with `gear.emit`. Any mod subscribes with `gear.on(name, fn)`, or with `gear.on('prefix.*', fn)` for every event of a mod (the handler then gets the event name first). Rules: the name is `<mod>.<what>` (`bounty.completed`), the payload is one table (new fields may be added, never removed or renamed), handlers must not change it, and a handler's error never reaches the publisher. Subscribing needs no dependency: a handler for an event nobody emits just never runs, so the load order does not matter. Each computer emits for what happens on it (in a network game every player's mod fires its own hero's hooks). The mods' hooks are listed in the documentation of the mod that publishes them; the game server's Lua mods use the same names and payloads.

### GearEventInfo

A declared hook.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `mod` | `string` | The id of the mod that declared it. |
| `doc` | `string` | When it fires. |
| `args` | `string` | The fields of the payload. |
| `listeners` | `integer` | How many handlers are subscribed now. |

### GearEventDecl

What `declare` takes.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` | `string` | When the hook fires. (optional) |
| `args` | `string` | The fields of the payload table. (optional) |

### GearEvents

Reached as `gear.events`.

The hook registry.

#### `gear.events.declare(name, info)`

Says that this mod emits `name` (`bounty.completed`). Declaring twice is fine; another mod's name is refused. The declaration ends when the mod unloads.

- `name`: `string`
- `info`: `GearEventDecl|string` (optional)

#### `gear.events.list(prefix) -> GearEventInfo[]`

The declared hooks, by name, optionally only those starting with `prefix` (`'bounty.'`).

- `prefix`: `string` (optional)
- returns `GearEventInfo[]`

#### `gear.events.declared(name) -> boolean`

Whether a loaded mod has declared `name`.

- `name`: `string`
- returns `boolean`

## Drawing (gear.ui)

### GearColor

A color: an `0xAARRGGBB` number (see `gear.ui.rgba`), `{r, g, b, a}` or `{r = , g = , b = , a = }` (0..255, `a` defaults to 255).

`integer|integer[]|{r: integer, g: integer, b: integer, a: integer?}`

### GearLayer

Where in the game's draw order. `world`: in game, over the world and under every window. `hud` (default): over the game's windows, under tooltips, the escape menu and message boxes. `top`: over everything but the cursor and its tooltip.

`'world'|'hud'|'top'`

### GearTextAlign

`'left'|'center'|'right'`

### GearTextVAlign

`'top'|'middle'|'bottom'|'baseline'`

### GearImageFit

`'stretch'|'contain'|'cover'|'fit'|'fill'`

### GearDrawOpts

Options of every draw function.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `layer` | `GearLayer` | Default `'hud'`. (optional) |
| `window` | `string` | A control name (`UI_WND_INVENTORY`): the command is drawn in that window's coordinates and frame, so it moves with the window, and clipped to its 1024x768 frame; nothing is drawn while the window does not exist. (optional) |

### GearTextOpts

Includes everything of `GearDrawOpts`.

Options of `gear.ui.text` (and the font options of widgets and `text_size`).

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `color` | `GearColor` | Default white. (optional) |
| `font` | `'ui'\|'game1'\|'game2'\|'game3'\|'game4'\|'game5'\|'game6'\|'game7'\|integer` | Default: the vector UI font (Segoe UI). `'game1'`..`'game7'` (or the number 1..7; 0 is a debug font) draw in the game's own bitmap font, scaled with the UI. (optional) |
| `size` | `number` | The em height in layout units (vector font; default 13). (optional) |
| `face` | `string` | A Windows font name (vector font). (optional) |
| `bold` | `boolean` | Vector font. (optional) |
| `italic` | `boolean` | Vector font. (optional) |
| `shadow` | `boolean` | Vector font: a dark 1 pixel shadow. (optional) |
| `outline` | `boolean` | Vector font: a dark 1 pixel outline. (optional) |
| `width` | `number` | The box width, for `align`. (optional) |
| `height` | `number` | The box height, for `valign`. (optional) |
| `align` | `GearTextAlign` | Aligns in `width`. (optional) |
| `valign` | `GearTextVAlign` | Aligns in `height`; `'middle'` puts the capitals' middle on the box's, `'baseline'`: y is the first line's baseline. (optional) |
| `background` | `GearColor` | A rectangle behind the text, sized to it. (optional) |
| `padding` | `number` | Around the text, with `background`. (optional) |
| `markup` | `boolean` | Game fonts: pass their backslash codes (`\c` color, `\g` image) through; otherwise a `\` shows as `/`. (optional) |
| `flags` | `integer` | Raw font flags of the game's font (or-ed into `align`). (optional) |

### GearImageOpts

Includes everything of `GearDrawOpts`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `fit` | `GearImageFit` | `'stretch'` (default: fills the box), `'contain'` (the whole image, aspect kept, centered), `'cover'` (fills the box, aspect kept, the overhang cut off). (optional) |
| `flip` | `'h'\|'v'\|'hv'` | Mirrored left-right (`'h'`), upside down (`'v'`) or both. (optional) |
| `color` | `GearColor` | Tint: white as is; the alpha makes it translucent. (optional) |
| `crop` | `number[]` | `{left, top, right, bottom}` as fractions of the image (default `{0, 0, 1, 1}`): only that part is drawn, where it would be in the box. `{0, 0.6, 1, 1}` draws the lower 40 % (a gauge). (optional) |

### GearImageInfo

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `integer` | The game's image index (stable for a build). |
| `sheet` | `string` | The sheet's TGA name. |
| `width` | `integer` |  |
| `height` | `integer` |  |
| `loaded` | `boolean` |  |

### GearUi

Reached as `gear.ui`.

Drawing is immediate mode: what a mod draws during a tick (its `draw` and `frame` handlers, timers, tasks) is shown until the next tick replaces it, so a mod draws its overlay every frame, usually in a `draw` handler. Without a tick (a loading screen, the menus without automation) nothing is drawn after half a second.

Positions and sizes are the UI's 1024x768 layout, the space the game lays its windows out in; the game and SacredBild scale it to the screen. A mod may issue 2000 draw commands per tick (widgets count their rectangles and texts).

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `WIDTH` | `integer` | 1024 |
| `HEIGHT` | `integer` | 768 |
| `COLORS` | `GearColors` | The widgets' colours. |
| `native` | `GearUiNative` | Pieces of the game's own look built from its UI images (`gear.ui.native.frame`). |
| `rml` | `GearUiRml` | HTML/CSS-style documents (RmlUi): `gear.ui.rml.load`. |

### GearColors

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `bg` | `integer` |  |
| `bg_hover` | `integer` |  |
| `bg_down` | `integer` |  |
| `edge` | `integer` |  |
| `edge_dim` | `integer` |  |
| `text` | `integer` |  |
| `text_dim` | `integer` |  |
| `accent` | `integer` |  |
| `title` | `integer` |  |

#### `gear.ui.rgba(r, g, b, a) -> integer`

The color number `0xAARRGGBB` (`a` defaults to 255).

- `r`: `integer`
- `g`: `integer`
- `b`: `integer`
- `a`: `integer` (optional)
- returns `integer`

#### `gear.ui.rect(x, y, w, h, color, opts) -> boolean`

A filled rectangle (default color: black, 75 % opaque). Edges snap to the screen's pixels.

- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `h`: `number`
- `color`: `GearColor` (optional)
- `opts`: `GearDrawOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean` - False when nothing was drawn (its `window` does not exist).

#### `gear.ui.frame(x, y, w, h, color, thickness, opts) -> boolean`

An outline inside the box.

- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `h`: `number`
- `color`: `GearColor` (optional)
- `thickness`: `number` (optional) - Default 1.
- `opts`: `GearDrawOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.text(text, x, y, opts) -> boolean`

Text, UTF-8, lines break at `\n`. By default in a vector UI font (Segoe UI) rasterized for the screen's pixels, so it stays sharp however far the UI is scaled.

- `text`: `any` - Converted with `tostring`.
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearTextOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.image(id, x, y, w, h, opts) -> boolean`

A UI image; `w`, `h` default to its own size. Images are filtered linearly.

- `id`: `integer` - An id from `images`, or a picture id (`gear.game.save_picture`).
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number` (optional)
- `h`: `number` (optional)
- `opts`: `GearImageOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.item_icon(item, x, y, w, h, opts) -> boolean`

What the game's inventory windows show for an item, its own 3D model, drawn by the game's model renderer as large as fits the box (x, y, w, h) and centered in it (the inventory's own size is 32 units a cell). Give an item (a table from `gear.world.item` or a container's `items()`: the live object is drawn, with its own state), or a type id or name: then a temporary item of that type is made at the hero's feet for the frame and destroyed after the layer's drawing (a type id or name needs no item object: its model pair comes from the model loader; no tint). Same `layer` and `window` options as the other draws.

- `item`: `GearItem|integer|string` - An item, a type id or a type name.
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `h`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearDrawOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean` - False when it could not be queued (a bad window or layer); whether the model really draws is known to the game's renderer only.

#### `gear.ui.item_tooltip(item, x, y) -> boolean?, number|string?, number?`

The game's own tooltip popup for an item, as the inventory windows show it (framed, the name in the rarity colour, price, protection, level, bonus lines), centered on (x, y) of the 1024x768 layout and kept on the screen. `item` is an item (a table from `gear.world.item` or a container's `items()`), an item id, or the string `gear.inv.export` made (a temporary item is made to read the text from and destroyed at once, local-only in a network game). Call it every frame the tooltip should be shown; it is drawn by the game's popup pass. `x`, `y` are the popup's top-left corner. It also returns the popup's size as of its last layout (what the previous tooltip it showed took; 0 at first), so a mod can place the next one beside a region.

- `item`: `GearItem|integer|string`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`
- returns `width_or_error` `number|string?` - The popup's width in layout units, or the message when `ok` is nil.
- returns `height` `number?`

#### `gear.ui.item_tooltip_text(item) -> string?, string?`

The words of the game's item tooltip (UTF-8, with the game's colour codes such as `\c...`) instead of a popup, for the same arguments as `item_tooltip`. Reading an export needs no registered object: a scratch item the object factory makes is filled with the data, asked and deleted, with no object id, no object manager and nothing sent to the network.

- `item`: `GearItem|integer|string`
- returns `text` `string?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.ui.hovered_item() -> GearItem?, number?, number?, number?, number?`

The item whose tooltip the game shows right now: the cursor (the mouse's or the controller's pad cursor) rests on an item in the backpack, the chest, a shop, the equipment window ... Read as of the last frame; nil when no item tooltip is up. Also returns the tooltip's visible outer rectangle (top-left corner and size of the frame's bars; the corner ornaments reach a few units beyond it) in the same layout units `gear.ui.*` draws in, so a mod can put something beside it (see `tooltip_anchor`). The game's own popup numbers are in another space (the canvas, whose origin is the screen's left edge instead of the layout's) and a little smaller than the frame; Sacred Gear converts them.

- returns `item` `GearItem?`
- returns `x` `number?`
- returns `y` `number?`
- returns `w` `number?`
- returns `h` `number?`

### GearTooltipAnchorOpts

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `gap` | `number` | More space between the two frames than the touching ornaments (default 0). (optional) |
| `margin` | `number` | Distance kept from the screen's edges (default 2). (optional) |
| `side` | `'right'\|'left'` | Force a side; by default the right one, the left one when the panel does not fit on the right. (optional) |

#### `gear.ui.tooltip_anchor(w, h, opts) -> number?, number?, ('right'|'left')?`

Where a panel goes to sit flush against the game's item tooltip: the top-left corner `x`, `y` of a panel whose frame's bars are `w` x `h` (what `gear.ui.native.frame` takes), beside the tooltip `hovered_item` reports, with the corner ornaments of both frames touching. On the right of the tooltip, on its left when it does not fit, never outside the screen, its top level with the tooltip's (moved up or down to fit). nil when no item tooltip is up. Also returns the side used.

- `w`: `number`
- `h`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearTooltipAnchorOpts` (optional)
- returns `x` `number?`
- returns `y` `number?`
- returns `side` `('right'|'left')?`

#### `gear.ui.texture_image(name) -> integer?`

A texture of the game's Texture.pak by its file name (`GUI_MOVE_RUNDUM.TGA`, any case) as an image id for `image`; nil if the game has none. The engine loads it and it keeps its own size. The icons of combat arts and spells are such textures (`gear.classes.art_icon`).

- `name`: `string`
- returns `id` `integer?`

#### `gear.ui.images(filter) -> GearImageInfo[]`

The UI images whose sheet name contains `filter` (any case), all of them without a filter.

- `filter`: `string` (optional)
- returns `GearImageInfo[]`

#### `gear.ui.image_info(id) -> GearImageInfo?`

One UI image, or nil.

- `id`: `integer`
- returns `GearImageInfo?`

#### `gear.ui.fonts() -> integer`

The number of the game's UI fonts.

- returns `integer`

#### `gear.ui.text_size(text, font) -> number?, number?`

Width and height of the text in the layout, or nil. Game fonts in game only (measuring may add glyphs to the font).

- `text`: `any`
- `font`: `'ui'|'game1'|'game2'|'game3'|'game4'|'game5'|'game6'|'game7'|integer|GearTextOpts` (optional) - A game font, or a table of `text`'s font options; nil: the default UI font.
- returns `width` `number?`
- returns `height` `number?`

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.capture_keys(on)`

While `on`, the keyboard does not reach the game: its key and character messages are dropped (with the release of every key whose press was dropped) and its key state queries see nothing held, so hotkeys and typing stay out of the game. The mod's own `key_pressed` and `key_down` still work, the mouse is not affected. For a screen that types or binds keys; it ends when the mod unloads. Not tied to `gear.keys`: declared keys of other mods stay quiet only for the Mods screen.

- `on`: `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.typed() -> string`

What the player typed since the last tick while this mod captures the keys (`capture_keys`): the characters their keyboard layout makes (umlauts, Shift, AltGr), UTF-8, no control characters (read Backspace and Enter with `key_pressed`). Empty otherwise. For a text field.

- returns `string`

#### `gear.ui.key_down(name) -> boolean`

Whether the key is held.

- `name`: `GearKey`
- returns `boolean`

## The game's own look (gear.ui.native)

### GearUiNative

Reached as `gear.ui.native`.

Pieces of the game's own look, drawn with its UI images (`gear.ui.images`) through `gear.ui.image` and `gear.ui.rect`: layers, windows, the draw command budget and the 1024x768 layout work as for those. Nothing here needs a game font; the text is the mod's. A style is a table of image ids and sizes inside Sacred Gear, so a further piece (a ring, a bar) is one more style.

### GearNativeFrameOpts

Includes everything of `GearDrawOpts`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `'tooltip'\|'thick'` | The frame style: `'tooltip'` (default) is the border of the game's item tooltip, dark metal bars with ornaments in the four corners (image 54 top-left, 55 top-right, flipped upside down at the bottom; 52 for the bars). `'thick'` is the heavy ornate frame of the character selection and the other big menu screens: rounded corner pieces (images 318 to 321) at the corners of the box, pattern strips between them (294, with 310 and 312 down the sides), crests on the middle of the top and bottom edge (302 to 305); the fill stays inside the strips (22 units from the sides, 25 from the top, 28 from the bottom) so the scene shows through between the strips and the fill, as in the game. The box is the outer rectangle of the corner pieces; there is no overhang. (optional) |
| `fill_inset` | `number\|number[]` | `'thick'` only: where the fill starts, measured from the box edge: one number for all sides or `{left, top, right, bottom}`. The game sets it per window: the character selection and the settings 22, 24.5, 22, 24.5 (the default: the fill touches the thin brown line inside the strips on all four sides), the popup dialog about 16, 20.5, 15, 17.5, the in-game menu about 20.5 / 22 / 20.5 (bottom not measured). Through RmlUi: `data-fill-inset="16"` or `data-fill-inset="16 20.5 15 17.5"`. (optional) |
| `dividers` | `number[]` | `'thick'` only: offsets from the top of the box to the top of a divider (a repeated strip, image 294) between the sides. (optional) |
| `fill` | `GearColor\|false` | The fill inside the bars (default the game's translucent black `0x9F000000`); `false` draws none. (optional) |
| `color` | `GearColor` | Tint of the border images (white as is). (optional) |

#### `gear.ui.native.frame(x, y, w, h, opts) -> boolean`

A frame in the game's own style: the fill, the four bars and the four corner ornaments. `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` are the bars' outer rectangle (the fill's too); the corner ornaments reach a few units beyond it (see `insets`), like the game's tooltip, whose own frame is this one. Put the contents inside `x + inset.left` ... and leave `overhang` of room if the ornaments must not cover anything.

- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `h`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearNativeFrameOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.native.insets(style) -> {left: number, top: number, right: number, bottom: number}, {left: number, top: number, right: number, bottom: number}`

How far the border of a frame style reaches into its box (the text goes inside that) and how far its corner ornaments reach out of the box, both as `{left, top, right, bottom}` in layout units.

- `style`: `'tooltip'|'thick'` (optional) - Default `'tooltip'`.
- returns `inset` `{left: number, top: number, right: number, bottom: number}`
- returns `overhang` `{left: number, top: number, right: number, bottom: number}`

## HTML/CSS documents (gear.ui.rml)

### GearUiRml

Reached as `gear.ui.rml`.

UI written as documents (RmlUi's HTML and CSS dialect: `.rml` and `.rcss` files with `div`, `button`, `input`, flexbox, `:hover` and animations) in the mod's own folder. A document is loaded once and drawn every frame from a `draw` handler with `doc:draw()`; its buttons, links and inputs take the mouse and the controller (every one is a pad stop), a focused text field takes the keyboard, and events (`click`, `change` ...) call Lua functions registered with `doc:on`. The default font is Segoe UI, as for `gear.ui` text; `rml.load_font` adds the mod's own. Images: a file of the mod's folder (PNG, TGA, JPG), or the game's own UI images as `gear:image/<id>` (`gear.ui.images`, or a picture id of Gear's own such as `gear.game.save_picture`'s: a savegame's thumbnail, drawn as it is, kept by the mod, not released with the document) `gear:texture/<NAME.TGA>` (Texture.pak) and an item's own model, as the game's inventory windows show it, as `gear:item/<item type id>` (a temporary item of that type, single player only) or `gear:item/id/<item object id>` (a live item; no tint or CSS transform, drawn as large as fits the box of the element, only while the whole box lies inside its clip, so a scrolled list hides the icons it cuts), with `?flip=h`, `?flip=v` or `?flip=hv` mirroring them, `?point` sampling them with the nearest texel instead of the bilinear filter (a picture scaled up stays crisp: `gear:image/54?point`): `<img src="gear:image/54">`, `decorator: image(gear:image/54)`. Button prompts of the controller (needs Sacred Bild; the glyphs of the pad in use) as `gear:pad/<button>` (`a b x y lb rb lt rt back start l3 r3 up down left right`, also `confirm` = a, `cancel` = b, `menu` = start): `<img src="gear:pad/a"/>` in front of the label, sized in `em` so it follows the text. `doc:draw` sets the classes `pad` (the controller was used last), `pad-ps` and `pad-switch` (the pad's style) on `<body>`, so a stylesheet shows the prompts only while they matter (the theme mod below ships that rule): `.padkey { display: none; } body.pad .padkey { display: inline-block; }`. The icon is chosen when the image loads, so it follows the pad's style from the next load on. Theme: a running mod whose `mod.lua` has `theme = 'file.rcss'` provides the shared stylesheet (classes for windows, buttons, fields, lists, bars, pad prompts); Gear puts it in front of every document's own styles, so documents only override; `{theme = false}` in the load options opts out. Data binding: load with `{model = {...}, calls = {...}}` and write `<body data-model="model">` with `{{ expression }}`, `data-value`, `data-if`, `data-for`, `data-class-x`, `data-attr-x` (the attribute's text: a false value is still the text "false", so the attribute is there), `data-attrif-x` (a flag attribute such as `checked` or `disabled`: set while the expression is true, removed while it is false) and `data-event-click="name(args)"`. Rings: `<gear-ring value="0.4" thickness="3" on="#e0c040" off="#40404080" start="0" dots="0" segments="96"/>` is an element that draws a ring (or, with `dots="n"`, a ring of n dots) in the size of its CSS box (`display: inline-block; width; height`), lit clockwise from the top (`start` degrees further round) for the fraction `value` (0 to 1) of its circle in the `on` colour, the rest in `off` (`#rgb`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`): `data-attr-value="time_left / total"` makes it follow the data model; change values with `doc.model.key = value` (nested writes work too) and the document refreshes only what depends on them.

Controller prompts: every `button` that has no `.padkey` child gets `<span class="padkey a">` (the confirm prompt, shown while the pad is on that button; the themes and the base style show it only then), and every RmlUi control is a stop that draws its own prompt: Sacred Bild draws none beside it. A `.padkey` of another button (`b`, `y`, `lb` ...) is the shortcut of the control and becomes the confirm prompt while the pad is on it; `data-no-padkey` on a button keeps it without one. Scroll bars of boxes that scroll take the mouse (knob drag, groove, arrows); stops are in stacking order (a `z-index` list over rows takes the pad and the mouse first). A prototype: no JavaScript (the logic is Lua), no filters, shaders, blur or drop shadows yet (CSS `transform` works: 2D rotate, scale, skew, translate and perspective, applied to the vertices; the mouse and the pad still hit the untransformed boxes), and a mesh counts as a draw command (at most 1500 per document and draw). The document's windows (its top-level elements) take the mouse where they are; the rest of the canvas stays the game's. Documents are laid out in the 1024x768 layout; `dp = true` lays them out in screen pixels instead (1dp is one layout unit), so text is crisp at any resolution (write sizes in `dp` then).

### GearRmlLoadOpts

The options of `load` and `load_string`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `theme` | `boolean` | `false`: do not add the theme mod's stylesheet to this document. Default: added. (optional) |
| `model` | `table` | Data binding: the values of the document's data model, named `model` (`<body data-model="model">`, then `{{ hp }}`, `data-value="name"`, `data-if="hp < 10"`, `data-for="item : items"`, `data-class-low="hp < 10"` ...). Top-level keys fix what can be bound; their values may be numbers, strings, booleans, lists and records (nested up to 8 deep). Change them through `doc.model`. (optional) |
| `calls` | `table<string, fun(args: string[], doc: GearRmlDoc, event: GearRmlEvent)>` | Functions for `data-event-click="name(arg, ...)"` attributes; `args` are the call's arguments as text. (optional) |
| `on_change` | `fun(doc: GearRmlDoc, model: table)` | Called after the document changed a value itself (an input with `data-value`); the table is up to date. (optional) |
| `dp` | `boolean` | Lay the document out in screen pixels with `1dp` = one layout unit (crisp text; write sizes in `dp`). Default `false`: `1px` = one layout unit, text is scaled with the UI. (optional) |

### GearRmlDrawOpts

The options of `GearRmlDoc.draw`. A top-level element with `position: absolute` and `data-panel="name"` (and optionally `data-title="Title"`) is a window the player can move in the layout editor, like a `gear.ui.panel`; its place is kept under the layout key `<mod id>:name`. Add `data-resizable` (and optionally `data-min-width` / `data-min-height`, layout units, default 120 / 60) and the editor sizes it too (a corner grip, or the numbers in its popup); the size is kept with the place and applied as the element's border box. A list that scrolls (`overflow-y: auto`) and has the attribute `data-nav-scroll` is a scroll area for the controller: the D-pad's up / down walk its cards (buttons, links) one by one, and at the edge of the view scroll the list by exactly the distance to the next card, so the cursor is on it; a card that is only partly in view under the cursor is scrolled fully into view. Elements scrolled out of sight (their centre outside an ancestor that clips) are no pad stops in any document.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `layer` | `'world'\|'hud'\|'top'` | Default `'hud'`. (optional) |
| `modal` | `boolean` | Draw the document as a modal dialog: while it is drawn with `modal = true`, the game and every other overlay (of any mod) take no mouse and no pad focus. Use `layer = 'top'`. (optional) |

### GearRmlEvent

An event delivered to a `GearRmlDoc.on handler.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `string` | The event's name (`'click'`, `'change'` ...). |
| `target` | `string` | The `id` of the element the event happened on (`''` if it has none). |
| `current` | `string` | The `id` of the element the handler listens on. |
| `params` | `table<string, string>` | The event's parameters as text; a form control's `change` has `value`, mouse events `mouse_x` and `mouse_y`. |

### GearRmlElement

An element of a document: a handle, found with `GearRmlDoc.query`. If it is removed (or the markup around it replaced), its methods answer nothing instead of failing.

#### `GearRmlElement:exists() -> boolean`

Whether the element is still in the document.

- returns `boolean`

#### `GearRmlElement:tag() -> string?`

The element's tag name (`'div'`), nil if it is gone.

- returns `string?`

#### `GearRmlElement:query(selector) -> GearRmlElement?`

The first descendant matching a CSS selector.

- `selector`: `string`
- returns `GearRmlElement?`

#### `GearRmlElement:query_all(selector) -> GearRmlElement[]`

All descendants matching a CSS selector (at most 500).

- `selector`: `string`
- returns `GearRmlElement[]`

#### `GearRmlElement:parent() -> GearRmlElement?`

The parent element (nil for a top-level element).

- returns `GearRmlElement?`

#### `GearRmlElement:children() -> GearRmlElement[]`

The child elements (at most 500).

- returns `GearRmlElement[]`

#### `GearRmlElement:append(tag, attrs) -> GearRmlElement?`

Adds a new empty element as the last child; fill it with `html` / `text`, or `append` to it.

- `tag`: `string`
- `attrs`: `table<string, any>` (optional) - Attributes, e.g. `{class = 'item', id = 'row1'}`.
- returns `child` `GearRmlElement?`

#### `GearRmlElement:remove() -> boolean`

Takes the element out of the document. Returns whether it was there.

- returns `boolean`

#### `GearRmlElement:html(markup) -> string?`

The element's inner markup; with an argument it is replaced.

- `markup`: `string` (optional)
- returns `string?`

#### `GearRmlElement:text(text) -> string?`

The element's content; with an argument it is replaced by that text (markup characters are escaped).

- `text`: `string` (optional)
- returns `string?`

#### `GearRmlElement:attr(name, value) -> string?`

An attribute's text; with a value it is set (`true` sets a flag such as `disabled`, `false` removes the attribute).

- `name`: `string`
- `value`: `string|number|boolean` (optional)
- returns `string?`

#### `GearRmlElement:class(name, on) -> boolean`

Switches a class on or off.

- `name`: `string`
- `on`: `boolean`
- returns `found` `boolean`

#### `GearRmlElement:style(property, value) -> boolean`

Sets an inline style; nil or false takes it off again.

- `property`: `string`
- `value`: `string|number|false` (optional)
- returns `found` `boolean`

#### `GearRmlElement:value(text) -> string?`

The value of a form control; with an argument it is set.

- `text`: `string|number` (optional)
- returns `string?`

#### `GearRmlElement:rect() -> {x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number}?`

The element's box in layout units.

- returns `{x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number}?`

#### `GearRmlElement:focus(on) -> boolean?`

Gives the element the focus (a text field then takes the keyboard until the focus moves), or with `false` takes the focus away.

- `on`: `boolean` (optional) - Default true.
- returns `focused` `boolean?` - Whether the element has the focus now (nil if it is gone).

#### `GearRmlElement:scroll(to) -> number?, number?, number?`

The scroll position of a box with `overflow: auto` or `scroll`, in layout units, after moving it when `to` is given: a number (the top of the visible part), `'start'`, or `'end'` (the bottom of the content: a chat window that sticks to its newest line scrolls to `'end'` while it was at the end).

- `to`: `number|'start'|'end'` (optional)
- returns `top` `number?` - The scroll position (nil if the element is gone).
- returns `height` `number?` - The height of the content.
- returns `client` `number?` - The height of the visible part.

#### `GearRmlElement:on(event, fn) -> boolean`

Calls `fn(event, element)` when the event happens on the element or inside it, also for elements added later (the listener sits on the document and matches when the event arrives).

- `event`: `string`
- `fn`: `fun(event: GearRmlEvent, element: GearRmlElement)`
- returns `ok` `boolean`

### GearRmlDoc

A loaded document.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | `table` | The data model's values (when loaded with `model`): read and write them like a table, at any depth; a write refreshes the bindings of the document. (optional) |

#### `GearRmlDoc:query(selector) -> GearRmlElement?`

The first element matching a CSS selector.

- `selector`: `string`
- returns `GearRmlElement?`

#### `GearRmlDoc:query_all(selector) -> GearRmlElement[]`

All elements matching a CSS selector (at most 500).

- `selector`: `string`
- returns `GearRmlElement[]`

#### `GearRmlDoc:get(key) -> any`

The plain value of a top-level key of the data model (a table for lists and records).

- `key`: `string`
- returns `any`

#### `gear.ui.rml.load(path, opts) -> GearRmlDoc?, string?`

Loads a document of the mod's folder.

- `path`: `string` - A `.rml` file in the mod's folder; its stylesheets and images are read from there too.
- `opts`: `GearRmlLoadOpts` (optional)
- returns `doc` `GearRmlDoc?`
- returns `message` `string?` - Why not.

#### `gear.ui.rml.load_string(markup, opts) -> GearRmlDoc?, string?`

Loads a document from a string of RML (relative links resolve in the mod's folder).

- `markup`: `string`
- `opts`: `GearRmlLoadOpts` (optional)
- returns `doc` `GearRmlDoc?`
- returns `message` `string?`

#### `gear.ui.rml.load_font(path, fallback) -> boolean`

Adds a font file of the mod (TTF or OTF) for `font-family` in the documents.

- `path`: `string`
- `fallback`: `boolean` (optional) - Use it for characters the other fonts lack.
- returns `ok` `boolean`

### GearRmlFont

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `family` | `string` | The name for `font-family`. |
| `real` | `boolean` | True when the family comes from its real file, false when it is the fallback (the family name still works). |
| `file` | `string` | The file the regular face comes from. |

#### `gear.ui.rml.fonts() -> {default: GearRmlFont, game: GearRmlFont, start: GearRmlFont}?`

The font families Sacred Gear registers for documents: `default` is `Segoe UI` (Arial under that name if Segoe is missing), `game` is `Sacred Game` (the game's own `ANTQS__.TTF` from the `font` folder next to Sacred.exe; the default face when that file is missing) and `start` is `Sacred Start` (`CAROLING.TTF`, the start screen's; else the game font). A stylesheet can always say `font-family: Sacred Game`; the theme's classes `font-game`, `font-default` and `font-start` use them. Nil before RmlUi could start.

- returns `{default: GearRmlFont, game: GearRmlFont, start: GearRmlFont}?`

#### `gear.ui.rml.game_font() -> string, boolean`

The family name of the game's own font and whether it is the real file (false: the fallback is registered under that name).

- returns `family` `string`
- returns `real` `boolean`

#### `GearRmlDoc:on(selector, event, fn) -> boolean`

Calls `fn(event, doc)` when `event` happens on an element that matches `selector`, or inside one (the innermost match is reported). Elements added later are covered too: the listener sits on the document and matches when the event arrives.

- `selector`: `string` - `'#id'`, `'.class'`, a tag, `'button.primary'` ... ; `''` is the document.
- `event`: `string` - `'click'`, `'change'`, `'submit'`, `'keydown'`, `'mouseover'`, `'focus'` ...
- `fn`: `fun(event: GearRmlEvent, doc: GearRmlDoc)`
- returns `ok` `boolean`

#### `GearRmlDoc:draw(opts) -> integer`

Runs the document for this frame and draws it: call it every frame from a `draw` handler. It takes the mouse over the document's windows, registers its buttons, links and inputs as pad stops, feeds a focused text field the keys, runs animations, calls the handlers of what happened and records the draw commands.

- `opts`: `GearRmlDrawOpts` (optional)
- returns `commands` `integer` - How many draw commands it recorded.

#### `GearRmlDoc:html(selector, markup) -> string?`

The inner markup of the first element matching `selector` (set it with `markup`); `nil` if there is none.

- `selector`: `string`
- `markup`: `string` (optional)
- returns `string?`

#### `GearRmlDoc:text(selector, text) -> string?`

The inner markup of the first element matching `selector`; with `text` its content becomes that text (escaped).

- `selector`: `string`
- `text`: `string|number` (optional)
- returns `string?`

#### `GearRmlDoc:attr(selector, name, value) -> string?`

An attribute of the first matching element. `value` sets it (`true` for a flag such as `disabled` or `checked`); `false` removes it.

- `selector`: `string`
- `name`: `string`
- `value`: `string|number|boolean` (optional)
- returns `current` `string?`

#### `GearRmlDoc:class(selector, name, on) -> boolean`

Adds or removes a class of the first matching element.

- `selector`: `string`
- `name`: `string`
- `on`: `boolean`
- returns `found` `boolean`

#### `GearRmlDoc:style(selector, property, value) -> boolean`

Sets an inline style property of the first matching element (`doc:style('#bar', 'width', '40%')`); `nil` or `false` takes it off.

- `selector`: `string`
- `property`: `string`
- `value`: `string|number|false` (optional)
- returns `found` `boolean`

#### `GearRmlDoc:value(selector, text) -> string?`

The value of a form control (an `input`, `select` or `textarea`); with `text` it is set.

- `selector`: `string`
- `text`: `string|number` (optional)
- returns `string?`

#### `GearRmlDoc:show()`

Shows the document again after `hide` (a loaded document is shown).

#### `GearRmlDoc:hide()`

Hides the document: it is not drawn and takes no mouse.

#### `GearRmlDoc:close()`

Closes the document. The mod's documents are closed when it unloads.

## Widgets and input

Widgets are immediate mode too: call them every frame with the current values; each draws itself, takes the mouse over its rectangle and returns what the player did since the last frame. `id` names the widget within the mod (any string or number, unique per widget). Positions are canvas coordinates (not `opts.window`).

### GearWidgetOpts

Options every widget takes.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `tooltip` | `string` | Shown after the cursor rests on the widget for 0.4 s. (optional) |
| `layer` | `GearLayer` | Default `'hud'`. (optional) |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `false`: greyed out, no clicks. (optional) |
| `nav` | `boolean` | Default true (regions and every widget): a stop of the controller's D-pad. `false` for rectangles that only take the mouse (backgrounds, blockers). (optional) |

### GearLabelOpts

Includes everything of `GearWidgetOpts`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `font` | `'ui'\|'game1'\|'game2'\|'game3'\|'game4'\|'game5'\|'game6'\|'game7'\|integer` |  (optional) |
| `size` | `number` |  (optional) |
| `face` | `string` |  (optional) |
| `bold` | `boolean` |  (optional) |
| `italic` | `boolean` |  (optional) |
| `height` | `number` |  (optional) |
| `valign` | `GearTextVAlign` |  (optional) |
| `color` | `GearColor` |  (optional) |

### GearButtonOpts

Includes everything of `GearWidgetOpts`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `image` | `integer` | A UI image beside the text. (optional) |

### GearRadioGroupOpts

Includes everything of `GearWidgetOpts`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `horizontal` | `boolean` | Lay the options out in a row. (optional) |
| `spacing` | `number` | Between the options (default 18 vertical, 8 horizontal). (optional) |
| `tooltips` | `string[]` | One per option. (optional) |

### GearDropdownOpts

Includes everything of `GearWidgetOpts`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `max_rows` | `integer` | The open list shows at most this many entries and scrolls (default 12). (optional) |
| `height` | `number` | The closed box's height (default 18): 22 matches a 22 high button in the same row. (optional) |

### GearScrollOpts

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `step` | `number` | One line: Up / Down, an arrow button and the D-pad move it, a wheel notch three (default 20). (optional) |
| `layer` | `GearLayer` | Default `'hud'`. (optional) |
| `nav` | `boolean` | `false`: the area is no stop of the controller's D-pad. (optional) |

### GearScrollArea

What `scroll_begin` returns: the viewport (without the scrollbar) and where the content starts.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | `number` |  |
| `y` | `number` |  |
| `w` | `number` | The viewport's width (the area's, less the scrollbar when it shows). |
| `h` | `number` |  |
| `offset` | `number` | How far the content is scrolled (0 .. max). |
| `max` | `number` |  |
| `content_x` | `number` | Where the content's top-left lies: draw at `content_y + its own y`. |
| `content_y` | `number` |  |

### GearSliderOpts

Includes everything of `GearWidgetOpts`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `step` | `number` | Default 1. (optional) |
| `format` | `string\|false` | A `string.format` format for the number shown (default `'%g'`); false: no number. (optional) |

### GearPanelOpts

Includes everything of `GearWidgetOpts`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `closable` | `boolean` | Default true: an X in the title bar. (optional) |
| `draggable` | `boolean` | Default true: the title bar drags it. (optional) |
| `resizable` | `boolean` | A corner grip resizes it. (optional) |
| `min_width` | `number` | Default 120. (optional) |
| `min_height` | `number` | Default 60. (optional) |
| `background` | `GearColor` |  (optional) |
| `back` | `boolean` | Default true: the controller's B closes the panel while it is the topmost closable one; `false`: the mod handles B itself (`ui.back_pressed`). (optional) |
| `bare` | `boolean` | No window: no background, frame, title bar, close button or resize grip, and no region, so the mouse and clicks go on to the game; the mod draws in the whole rectangle (`content_*` is the rect). It is still a panel for the layout: the layout editor moves it (and resizes it with `resizable`) and `set_panel_rect` works; the layout editor's mode draws its frame. For a HUD element. `closable` and `draggable` do not apply. (optional) |
| `passive` | `boolean` | A closable panel that should not take the controller (no cursor, B not caught): a HUD-like panel. (optional) |

### GearUiTableColumn

One column of a table. A bare number or string in `columns` is a column of that `width`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `width` | `number\|string` | A number: that many layout units. `'auto'`: as wide as the widest cell of the last frame (labels, buttons, checkboxes, dropdowns report their size; one frame late, so the first frame is `min` or 0), within `min` / `max`. `'*'` or `'2*'`: a share of what the fixed and auto columns and the gaps leave (default `'*'`). (optional) |
| `min` | `number` | For a share or auto column: never narrower. (optional) |
| `max` | `number` | For a share or auto column: never wider. (optional) |
| `align` | `GearTableHAlign` | Where the column's labels (and widgets of their own size) sit (default left). (optional) |
| `valign` | `GearTableVAlign` | The same vertically (default: labels and sized widgets centred, the rest stretch). (optional) |
| `title` | `string` | A header over the column; with any title the table draws a header row (bold, a line under it) by itself. (optional) |

`'left'|'center'|'right'|'stretch'`

`'top'|'center'|'middle'|'bottom'|'stretch'`

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `rows` | `boolean` | A line between rows. (optional) |
| `columns` | `boolean` | A line between columns (through every row: pass `{columns = false}` to `t:row` under a cell that spans columns). (optional) |
| `outer` | `boolean` | A frame around the table. (optional) |
| `color` | `GearColor` | Default the widgets' dim edge colour. (optional) |

### GearUiTableOpts

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `columns` | `(GearUiTableColumn\|number\|string)[]` |  |
| `spacing` | `number\|number[]` | Between the columns and the rows: one number, or `{columns, rows}` (default `{8, 4}`). (optional) |
| `row_height` | `number` | Default 22: as high as a button, so buttons, dropdowns and labels line up. (optional) |
| `header` | `boolean` | `false`: no header row even though columns have titles. (optional) |
| `header_height` | `number` | Default `row_height`. (optional) |
| `row_heights` | `number[]` | The heights of rows by number (body rows, from 1), for `t:row()` without a height and for the rows a `rowspan` cell reaches over. (optional) |
| `borders` | `boolean\|GearUiTableBorders` | Grid lines in the gaps between columns and rows and around the table (true: all three; the gaps should be at least 3 wide). Call `t:finish()` after the last row for the bottom line. (optional) |
| `stripes` | `boolean\|GearColor` | Shade every second row (true: a faint white). (optional) |
| `layer` | `GearLayer` | The layer of everything the table draws; default `'hud'`. (optional) |

### GearUiTableCellOpts

Includes everything of `GearWidgetOpts`.

The widgets' common options as the table's cells take them.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string\|integer` | The widget's id (default: the table's id, the row and the column, so give one when rows come and go and a widget has a state, like a dropdown's open list). (optional) |
| `span` | `integer` | Columns the cell covers (default 1). (optional) |
| `rowspan` | `integer` | Rows the cell reaches down over (default 1); the later rows count with `row_heights` or `row_height`, and you leave out those rows' cells in these columns. (optional) |
| `width` | `number` | A width of its own (default: stretches over the cell; checkboxes and sliders take theirs). (optional) |
| `height` | `number` | A height of its own (default: the row's, a checkbox 16, a slider 16). (optional) |
| `halign` | `GearTableHAlign` | Where a narrower widget sits; `'stretch'` fills the cell's width whatever `width` says (default: stretch for buttons and dropdowns without a `width`, else the column's `align`, else left). (optional) |
| `valign` | `GearTableVAlign` | The same vertically (default: centred when the widget has a height of its own, else stretch). (optional) |
| `align` | `GearTableHAlign` | Alias of `halign`. (optional) |

Includes everything of `GearLabelOpts`.
