### GearUiTable

A table: a grid for a window's rows, so that labels, buttons, dropdowns and checkboxes line up without hand-counted coordinates. It only places things: the widgets are the ordinary ones (same look, same controller stops, ids), nothing is kept between frames but the sizes `'auto'` columns and rows need, so build it every frame. Inside a scroll area pass `area.content_x`, `area.content_y` and `area.w`, and `t:height()` is the content height. Cells can span columns and rows, align and stretch both ways, columns and rows can size themselves to their cells (`'auto'`, from the last frame), and `borders` draws grid lines.

#### `GearUiTable:row(height, background, opts) -> integer`

Starts the next row, `height` high (default `row_heights[n]` or `row_height`; `'auto'`: as high as the tallest cell of this row in the last frame), with an optional background colour (`stripes` shades every second row by itself). Call it before the row's cells; the first call starts the first row under the header.

- `height`: `number|'auto'` (optional)
- `background`: `GearColor` (optional)
- `opts`: `{columns: boolean?}` (optional) - `columns = false`: no column lines through this row.
- returns `row` `integer` - The row's number, counted from 1 without the header.

#### `GearUiTable:column(col) -> number, number`

A column's x and width (canvas coordinates).

- `col`: `integer`
- returns `x` `number`
- returns `w` `number`

#### `GearUiTable:cell(col, span) -> number, number, number, number`

The rectangle of a cell in the current row (`span` columns with the gaps between them, `rowspan` rows down), for drawing or widgets of your own.

- `col`: `integer`
- `span`: `integer` (optional)
- `rowspan`: `integer` (optional)
- returns `x` `number`
- returns `y` `number`
- returns `w` `number`
- returns `h` `number`

#### `GearUiTable:height() -> number`

The height of the header and the rows so far, without a trailing gap: the content height for `scroll_end`, or what to place the next thing under.

- returns `number`

#### `GearUiTable:width() -> number`

The table's width: what it was given, or, made without one (`nil` or `'auto'`), its fixed and auto columns, the gaps and the share columns' minimums.

- returns `number`

#### `GearUiTable:finish() -> number`

Ends the table: draws the bottom line of `borders.outer` and returns the height. Call it after the last row when `borders.outer` is on.

- returns `height` `number`

#### `GearUiTable:label(col, text, opts) -> boolean`

A label in the current row's cell (vertically centred, the UI font).

- `col`: `integer`
- `text`: `any`
- `opts`: `GearUiTableLabelOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean`

#### `GearUiTable:button(col, text, opts) -> boolean`

A button that fills the cell (the row's height) unless `opts.width`, `height` or `align` say otherwise.

- `col`: `integer`
- `text`: `any`
- `opts`: `GearUiTableCellOpts|GearButtonOpts` (optional)
- returns `clicked` `boolean`

#### `GearUiTable:checkbox(col, text, checked, opts) -> boolean, boolean`

- `col`: `integer`
- `text`: `any`
- `checked`: `boolean`
- `opts`: `GearUiTableCellOpts` (optional)
- returns `changed` `boolean`
- returns `checked` `boolean`

#### `GearUiTable:dropdown(col, options, index, opts) -> boolean, integer`

A dropdown as wide as the cell and as high as the row, so it matches the buttons beside it.

- `col`: `integer`
- `options`: `string[]`
- `index`: `integer`
- `opts`: `GearUiTableCellOpts|GearDropdownOpts` (optional)
- returns `changed` `boolean`
- returns `index` `integer`

#### `GearUiTable:slider(col, min, max, value, opts) -> boolean, number`

A slider that fills the cell less the room for its number.

- `col`: `integer`
- `min`: `number`
- `max`: `number`
- `value`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearUiTableSliderOpts` (optional)
- returns `changed` `boolean`
- returns `value` `number`

#### `GearUiTable:image(col, image, opts) -> boolean`

An image in the cell (`fit` default `'contain'`).

- `col`: `integer`
- `image`: `integer`
- `opts`: `GearUiTableImageOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.region(id, x, y, w, h, opts) -> GearRegionState`

A rectangle that takes the mouse, for widgets of a mod's own. A left click (press and release) over a mod's region is taken from the game: neither its windows nor the world see it. Regions on the world and hud layers take nothing while the escape menu or a message box is up.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `h`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearWidgetOpts` (optional)
- returns `GearRegionState`

### GearTooltipRectOpts

Options of `tooltip_rect`.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | `number` | The point to keep clear (default: the cursor's hotspot). (optional) |
| `y` | `number` |  (optional) |
| `bounds` | `number[]` | `{left, top, right, bottom}` the tooltip must stay inside (default: the screen); pass a panel's rectangle to keep it in that panel. (optional) |
| `cursor` | `boolean` | `false`: the point has no cursor sprite below and right of it, so only a small gap is kept (default true). (optional) |

#### `gear.ui.tooltip_rect(w, h, opts) -> number, number`

Where to put a `w` x `h` tooltip, or any popup beside the cursor, so that it never lies under the game's cursor sprite (an arrow reaching about 30 x 38 layout units right and down of the hotspot) and stays inside the screen. The default place is below the cursor's tip, to its right; when that leaves `bounds` it flips to below-left, above-right, above-left, then beside the cursor, and as a last resort is clamped and pushed off the sprite. The widgets' `tooltip` option already uses it. Returns the top-left corner.

- `w`: `number`
- `h`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearTooltipRectOpts` (optional)
- returns `x` `number`
- returns `y` `number`

#### `gear.ui.label(id, text, x, y, opts) -> boolean`

Text in the widgets' look (the UI font), with a tooltip if `opts.tooltip`.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `text`: `any`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearLabelOpts` (optional)
- returns `drawn` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.button(id, x, y, w, h, text, opts) -> boolean`

True when clicked.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `h`: `number`
- `text`: `any`
- `opts`: `GearButtonOpts` (optional)
- returns `clicked` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.checkbox(id, x, y, text, checked, opts) -> boolean, boolean`

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `text`: `any`
- `checked`: `boolean`
- `opts`: `GearWidgetOpts` (optional)
- returns `changed` `boolean`
- returns `checked` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.radio(id, x, y, text, selected, opts) -> boolean`

True when clicked.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `text`: `any`
- `selected`: `boolean`
- `opts`: `GearWidgetOpts` (optional)
- returns `clicked` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.radio_group(id, x, y, options, index, opts) -> boolean, integer`

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `options`: `string[]`
- `index`: `integer` - The selected option (1-based).
- `opts`: `GearRadioGroupOpts` (optional)
- returns `changed` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.dropdown(id, x, y, w, options, index, opts) -> boolean, integer`

The open list is drawn after every draw handler, over all panels and text, on the top layer, and takes the mouse first; it shows at most `opts.max_rows` (12) entries and scrolls (wheel, scrollbar, keys, D-pad), the selected one in view when it opens. A click beside it closes it.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `options`: `string[]`
- `index`: `integer` - The selected option (1-based).
- `opts`: `GearDropdownOpts` (optional)
- returns `changed` `boolean`
- returns `index` `integer`

#### `gear.ui.scroll_begin(id, x, y, w, h, opts) -> GearScrollArea`

Starts a vertically scrollable area: until `scroll_end`, what is drawn is clipped to its viewport (rects, images, the UI font's text; the game's fonts and item models only when wholly inside) and regions are cut to it, so a widget scrolled out of sight takes no click. Draw the content at `content_y + its own y`. The wheel scrolls the area under the cursor (3 lines a notch), Up / Down / PageUp / PageDown / Home / End the one under the cursor or clicked last, the controller's D-pad (SacredBild) the one its cursor is in, once no widget lies further that way inside it, and the right stick as a wheel. The offset is kept per id for the session. Areas nest.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `h`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearScrollOpts` (optional)
- returns `area` `GearScrollArea`

#### `gear.ui.scroll_end(content_height) -> number, number`

Ends the innermost scroll area and draws its scrollbar (arrows, track: a click pages, thumb: drag it) when the content is taller than the viewport.

- `content_height`: `number` (optional) - The content's height (default: the last one given).
- returns `offset` `number`
- returns `max` `number`

#### `gear.ui.scroll_to(id, offset)`

Sets a scroll area's offset (clamped when it is drawn next).

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `offset`: `number`

#### `gear.ui.scroll_offset(id) -> number, number`

A scroll area's offset and its largest offset (as of its last frame); 0, 0 for an unknown id.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- returns `offset` `number`
- returns `max` `number`

#### `gear.ui.wheel() -> number, boolean`

The mouse wheel's notches over mod UI this tick (+ away from the player, as Windows counts them; 0: none; a notch is 1), and whether a scroll area already took them. Over a mod's widget the game does not get the wheel.

- returns `notches` `number`
- returns `taken` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.text_wrap(text, width, opts) -> string[], number`

The text broken into lines that fit `width` (at spaces; a word longer than the width gets a line of its own; `\n` breaks too), in the font of `opts` (as `text` takes it), and the lines' total height. Cached per text, width and font.

- `text`: `string`
- `width`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearTextOpts` (optional)
- returns `lines` `string[]`
- returns `height` `number`

#### `gear.ui.slider(id, x, y, w, min, max, value, opts) -> boolean, number`

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `min`: `number`
- `max`: `number`
- `value`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearSliderOpts` (optional)
- returns `changed` `boolean` - True while dragged.
- returns `value` `number`

#### `gear.ui.table(id, x, y, w, opts) -> GearUiTable`

A table layout for a window's rows: `local t = gear.ui.table('items', x, y, w, {columns = {{title = 'Name', width = '2*'}, '*', 70}})`, then per row `t:row()` and `t:label(1, ...)`, `t:dropdown(2, ...)`, `t:button(3, ...)`. Columns are fixed widths and shares of the rest (with min / max), the gaps and the row height are the table's, so everything in a column shares one left edge and widgets of a row one height. Immediate mode like the widgets: build it every frame. See `GearUiTable`.

- `id`: `string|integer` - Prefixes the ids of the cells' widgets.
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number|'auto'|nil` - Nil or `'auto'`: as wide as the fixed and auto columns need.
- `opts`: `GearUiTableOpts`
- returns `GearUiTable`

#### `gear.ui.panel(id, title, x, y, w, h, opts) -> GearPanel`

A window: its title bar drags it (the position is kept in the layout), its X closes it (`open` false). Draw the content in the returned rectangle.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `title`: `any`
- `x`: `number` - The default place (the layout's place wins).
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number`
- `h`: `number`
- `opts`: `GearPanelOpts` (optional)
- returns `GearPanel`

#### `gear.ui.nav_modal(on)`

The controller: while on, the mod's screen has the pad alone. Only its widgets are D-pad stops (the game's controls and other mods' are not), the cursor starts on its first widget, and B is `back_pressed()`. Switch it off when the screen closes (it is also dropped when the mod unloads).

- `on`: `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.replace_window(name, on) -> boolean, string?`

Replaces the game's window `name` with the mod's own screen: while the window is open, the game neither draws it nor gives it the mouse or the keys; it still opens and closes as it always does (hotkeys, the escape menu), so the game's state stays the one it expects. Names: the in-game windows by control name (`UI_WND_SAVEGAME`, ...) and the menus' screens `UI_MENU_MAIN`, `UI_MENU_CHARACTER`, `UI_MENU_OPTIONS`, `UI_MENU_LOADGAME`, `UI_MENU_NETWORK`. One mod per window. The game's window comes back by itself when the mod does not draw its screen: call `replaced` every tick it does; 1.5 s after the window opened without it, or 0.5 s after the last call, the game's window shows until it closes. A mod that is off or unloaded replaces nothing. `on = false` gives the window back.

- `name`: `string`
- `on`: `boolean` (optional)
- returns `ok` `boolean`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.ui.replaced(name) -> boolean`

Call it every tick the mod draws its screen for a replaced window: true while the game's window is open and the mod's screen takes its place (draw it then); false when the window is closed or the game's own shows.

- `name`: `string`
- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.window_open(name) -> boolean`

Whether the game's window (an in-game control name or a menu screen, as for `replace_window`) is open.

- `name`: `string`
- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.close_window(name) -> boolean`

Closes the game's window as its own Back button or Esc does (the savegame window in the menus brings the start menu back). False if it is not open.

- `name`: `string`
- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.back_pressed() -> boolean`

The controller's B was pressed: true once per press (consumed). B closes an open dropdown and the topmost closable panel by itself; a `nav_modal` screen or a panel with `back = false` asks here.

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.page_pressed() -> integer`

The controller's LB (-1) or RB (+1) was pressed while a `nav_modal` screen or a window of a mod is open: 0 when neither (consumed: once per press; both in one tick cancel out). The previous / next page, tab or step of that screen. Show the prompts next to what it switches (`<span class="padkey lb"></span>` / `rb` in an RmlUi document: they appear while the controller is in use).

- returns `integer`

#### `gear.ui.select_pressed() -> boolean`

The controller's Select / "-" button was pressed: true once per press (consumed, for whoever asks first). Ask only where it means something to the mod (the mod manager asks while the escape menu is open: it opens its screen).

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.menu_item(id, label, fn)`

An entry of the controller's mod menu (Sacred Gear's mod menu button, LT + LB by default): for a tool a player would otherwise reach with a hotkey, Alt or a small button. The keys a mod declares in mod.lua are listed there by themselves; calling it again with the same id changes the entry.

- `id`: `string`
- `label`: `string`
- `fn`: `fun()`

## Drag and drop between mods

One drag at a time, across mods. A source is a widget or region the mod already draws; a target is a region of any mod (or the world). While the player drags, every target says whether it takes the drag (`accept`), and a hint follows the cursor: the dragged thing's icon or label, a green `+` over a target that takes it, a red `×` over anything that does not (with the target's reason beside it), nothing over the source itself. A release over a valid target calls its `on_drop`; anywhere else, or Esc, or the pad's B, ends the drag without a drop. The press that started the drag is taken from the game (no world click), and the release is no click on the source. Controller: a click on a source (`carry`) picks the thing up, the D-pad then reaches only the targets that take it, a click on one puts it down, B cancels. (Dropping into the world is mouse only.)

### GearDrag

What is being dragged.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `string` | The kind of thing (`'combat_art'`, `'creature_type'` ...): targets accept by type. |
| `data` | `any` | What the source carries (any Lua value). |
| `label` | `string` |  (optional) |
| `icon` | `integer` |  (optional) |
| `source` | `string` | Id of the mod that started the drag. |
| `carry` | `boolean` | Picked up with the controller (click to put down) rather than dragged with the mouse. |

### GearDragSourceOpts

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `string` | Required. |
| `data` | `any` |  (optional) |
| `label` | `string` | Drawn at the cursor (in a small box) when there is no icon. (optional) |
| `icon` | `integer` | A UI image id drawn at the cursor. (optional) |
| `icon_size` | `number` | Default 32. (optional) |
| `threshold` | `number` | Cursor travel in layout units before a press becomes a drag. Default 6. (optional) |
| `carry` | `boolean` | `false`: no controller pick-up on a click. Default true. (optional) |
| `enabled` | `boolean` |  (optional) |
| `on_end` | `fun(drag: GearDrag, dropped: boolean)` | The drag ended (dropped on a target or not). (optional) |

#### `gear.ui.drag_source(id, result, opts) -> boolean`

Makes the region or widget `id` (drawn this tick, `result` is what `region` or the widget returned) a drag source. Call it after the widget every tick. Returns true while this source is the one being dragged (dim it).

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `result`: `table`
- `opts`: `GearDragSourceOpts`
- returns `dragging` `boolean`

### GearDropTargetOpts

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `accept` | `string\|string[]\|fun(drag: GearDrag): boolean\|string\|nil, string` | A type, a list of types, `'*'` (anything), or a function: `ok, text` (text: the hint when ok, the reason when not; a lone string means "no" and is the reason). Default: anything. (optional) |
| `hint` | `string` | Shown beside the cursor while it takes the drag. (optional) |
| `on_drop` | `fun(drag: GearDrag, info: {x: number, y: number})` | Called on a release over the target when it accepts. |

### GearDropState

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `dragging` | `boolean` | Whether something is being dragged now (false: nothing else is set). |
| `over` | `boolean` | The cursor is over this target. |
| `valid` | `boolean` | The target takes the drag (also while the cursor is elsewhere: highlight the free slots). |
| `reason` | `string` |  (optional) |

#### `gear.ui.drop_target(id, opts) -> GearDropState`

Makes the region `id` (drawn this tick) a drop target. Call it every tick after the region; while nothing is dragged it costs nothing and returns a shared read-only table. A click that puts a carried thing down also reaches the region as `clicked`: check `drag_active()` before acting on it.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `opts`: `GearDropTargetOpts`
- returns `GearDropState`

### GearWorldDropOpts

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `accept` | `string\|string[]\|fun(drag: GearDrag): boolean\|string\|nil, string` |  (optional) |
| `hint` | `string` |  (optional) |
| `on_drop` | `fun(drag: GearDrag, spot: {x: number, y: number, layer: integer, object_id: integer?})` | `spot` is the world point under the cursor (as `gear.world.cursor`); `gear.world.cursor()` also gives the object there. |

#### `gear.ui.world_drop(id, opts)`

The world takes drops of what `accept` allows while the cursor is on it (not on a game window or a mod's UI): a dev mod spawns the dragged creature there. Registered once (not every tick); the same id replaces it, `nil` removes it. Nothing else on the screen reacts to the drag, so the world only shows a green `+` (or a red `×` when nothing takes it).

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `opts`: `GearWorldDropOpts|nil`

#### `gear.ui.drag_active() -> GearDrag?`

The drag that is on, or nil.

- returns `GearDrag?`

#### `gear.ui.drag_cancel()`

Ends the drag this mod's source started, without a drop.

#### `gear.ui.show_panel(id, open)`

Opens or closes a panel. Whether a panel is open is kept in the layout (`mods\gear_layout.json`) and comes back at the next start: what a mod sets with `show_panel` in its `main.lua` is only the default for a first start, after that the player's last state wins. `persist_panel(id, false)` opts a panel out.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `open`: `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.persist_panel(id, on)`

Whether a panel's open / closed state is kept across starts (default: yes). Call it in `main.lua` with `false` for a panel that only makes sense with a state of the mod (a dialog, an on-screen keyboard); it then always starts as the mod sets it.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `on`: `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.panel_open(id) -> boolean`

- `id`: `string|integer`
- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.toggle_panel(id) -> boolean`

Opens a closed panel, closes an open one. Returns whether it is open now.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- returns `open` `boolean`

## Layout: persistent panels, movable game windows

Every panel has the id `mod_id:panel_id`. Where the player drags it (and how large they make it, with `opts.resizable`) is kept in `mods\gear_layout.json` and restored at the next start. Places are stored in a virtual 4096 x 4096 screen (the whole screen, whatever its resolution and aspect). The game's own windows are kept there too, as `game:UI_WND_INVENTORY` and so on. Moving game windows needs SacredBild's UI frames.

### GearPanelInfo

A panel as `gear.ui.panels` lists it.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `string` |  |
| `mod` | `string` |  |
| `id` | `string\|integer` |  |
| `title` | `string` |  |
| `x` | `number` |  |
| `y` | `number` |  |
| `w` | `number` |  |
| `h` | `number` |  |
| `resizable` | `boolean` |  |
| `min_width` | `number` |  |
| `min_height` | `number` |  |
| `layer` | `GearLayer` |  |

### GearLayoutEntry

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | `number` | In virtual units. |
| `y` | `number` |  |
| `w` | `number` |  (optional) |
| `h` | `number` |  (optional) |

#### `gear.ui.edit_mode() -> boolean`

The layout edit mode flag, for every mod (panels get a highlighted frame).

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.set_edit_mode(on)`

- `on`: `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.can_move_windows() -> boolean`

Whether the game's windows can be moved (needs SacredBild's UI frames).

- returns `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.panels() -> GearPanelInfo[]`

The panels of every mod drawn this tick (those not drawn yet: as of the last tick).

- returns `GearPanelInfo[]`

#### `gear.ui.set_panel_rect(key, x, y, w, h) -> boolean`

Puts any mod's panel at (x, y) of the canvas and, if it is resizable, makes it w x h (nil: the size stays); kept in the layout, taken the next time its mod draws it.

- `key`: `string`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- `w`: `number` (optional)
- `h`: `number` (optional)
- returns `found` `boolean` - False for an unknown panel.

#### `gear.ui.reset_panel(key) -> boolean`

A panel back to the place and size its mod gives it.

- `key`: `string`
- returns `found` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.set_window_position(name, x, y) -> boolean`

Puts game window `name` with its top-left corner at (x, y) of the canvas and keeps it in the layout. Any in-game window but those the game draws alone (world map, savegame, options, character export).

- `name`: `string`
- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- returns `ok` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.reset_window(name) -> boolean`

A game window back to its own place.

- `name`: `string`
- returns `found` `boolean`

#### `gear.ui.reset_layout(prefix)`

Forgets all places, or those whose key starts with `prefix` (e.g. `'game:'`).

- `prefix`: `string` (optional)

#### `gear.ui.layout() -> table<string, GearLayoutEntry>`

The stored places.

- returns `table<string, GearLayoutEntry>`

#### `gear.ui.to_virtual(x, y) -> number, number`

From the canvas to the virtual 4096 x 4096 screen.

- `x`: `number`
- `y`: `number`
- returns `vx` `number`
- returns `vy` `number`

#### `gear.ui.from_virtual(vx, vy) -> number, number`

- `vx`: `number`
- `vy`: `number`
- returns `x` `number`
- returns `y` `number`

### GearAuto

Reached as `gear.auto`.

For self tests and scripted runs without a player. `gear.auto` exists only when the game starts with `-gear-auto` (or `SACREDGEAR_AUTO=1`) and the mod's manifest says `automation = true`. The functions marked "in a task" wait, so they work only inside `gear.task`.

| `VK` | `table<string, integer>` | Key names to virtual key codes. |
| `instance` | `string` | The run's name (`-gear-instance`). |

The mouse wheel at the cursor, as `WM_MOUSEWHEEL`: + away from the player (scrolls up), - towards.

- `key`: `GearAutoKey`

Releases everything held.

#### `gear.auto.pad(nudge, back, menu)`

The controller without one: posts pad events as SacredBild's controller does (D-pad steps on a slider, B presses, mod menu button presses).

The controller's LB / RB without one: posts `pages` page steps (-1 previous, +1 next), read by `ui.page_pressed`.

The kinds of the stops Gear told the controller about in the last tick: 0 button, 1 slider, 2 scroll area (+ 4 scrolled to its top, + 8 to its bottom: the D-pad leaves the list there).

The first stop Gear reported to the controller in the last tick: where the pad's cursor starts when a screen opens (`data-nav-home` puts a stop there).

The D-pad's up (-1) / down (+1) steps in a scroll area (a list marked `data-nav-scroll`, or a `ui.scroll` area), as the controller posts them: they act at the game cursor (`gear.auto.move`).

The Select / "-" button without a controller: one press, read by `ui.select_pressed`.

In a task: moves, presses and releases with short pauses, as a player would. Client pixels.

In a task: presses and releases a key.

In a task: types text, one character at a time.

In a task: the client pixel for the UI layout point (x, y); the mapping is measured once by moving the cursor.

#### `gear.auto.widget(id, mod_id) -> number?, number?, number?, number?`

Where a mod's widget was drawn in the last tick (UI layout coordinates, as `ui_click` takes them), found by the id it was given (`gear.ui.button('save', ...)`, a table cell's `id`); clipped to its scroll area. Nil when it was not drawn.

- `id`: `string|integer`
- `mod_id`: `string` (optional) - The mod that drew it (default: this mod).
- returns `x` `number?`

#### `gear.auto.ui_click(x, y, button) -> boolean?, string?`

In a task: clicks a point in UI layout coordinates, or a node's center.

- `x`: `number|GearAutoUiNode`

- `button`: `GearMouseButton` (optional)
- returns `ok` `boolean?`

#### `gear.auto.load_save(slot) -> boolean?`

Loads savegame `slot` from the menus.

- `slot`: `integer`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`

#### `gear.auto.screenshot(name) -> boolean?`

Saves a screenshot (`.bmp`) of the game's back buffer into `GearAutomation\<instance>`. Name: letters, digits, `_ - .`.

- `name`: `string`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`

#### `gear.auto.engine_level_factor_start(level) -> boolean`

Starts the engine's own level function on a worker thread (the first of the `level.factor` hooks): the call goes through the hook, so a mod that handles `level.factor` answers it. For tests.

- `level`: `integer`
- returns `started` `boolean` - false if a call is running or the function was not found.

#### `gear.auto.engine_level_factor_result() -> integer?`

The integer the call started by `engine_level_factor_start` returned; nil until it is done.

- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.auto.engine_free_slot() -> integer?`

The number the game's own "first free savegame number" (the function a new savegame without a number asks) answers now: the engine's function itself, called through Gear's replacement, so it is not limited to 509 savegames. nil if it was not found.

- returns `integer?`

#### `gear.auto.site_hook_selftest_start() -> boolean`

Tests the stubs of the constant site hooks on two functions built in memory (`fmul dword [c]` and `fld dword [c]`, with the sites `selftest.fmul` and `selftest.fld` of the event `combat.constant`); a worker thread calls them when Lua is idle.

- returns `started` `boolean` - false if a test is running.

#### `gear.auto.site_hook_selftest_result() -> {fmul: number, fld: number, registers_kept: boolean, ability_store: integer, ability_add: integer, ability_edx: integer, ability_kept: boolean, damage: integer, effect_exit: integer, effect_entry0: integer, effect_entry1: integer, effect_counter: integer, bonus_int: integer, bonus_float: number, slot_byte: integer, branch_taken: integer, branch2_path: integer, branch2_eax: integer}?`

The result of the test: `fmul` and `fld` are st0 after the instruction (the answer of the mods, else vanilla 0.2 and 0.2 times 1.0), `registers_kept` whether eax, ecx and edx survived the stub. The `ability_*` fields test the `creature.ability` stubs on three functions built in memory (a store of 100, an add of 1000 and the computed block; a fake creature of type 77): the stored id, the amount added and edx after the block (vanilla 100, 1000 and 50 without an answer), `ability_kept` whether the registers survived. `damage` is the result of the `damage` stub on a function built in memory (12.4 rounds to 12 without an answer). The `effect_*` fields test the `effect.add` stub on a function built in memory with a fake effect list (the sum 3.5 for entry 0, the creature's counter 4): the exit taken (1 engine path, 2 next entry, 3 leave), both entries' values times 100 and the counter. `bonus_int` / `bonus_float` are what the `bonus.constant` stubs push on functions built in memory (`push 5` and `push 3.5`). `slot_byte` is 1 when the `skillslot.select` stub kept the displaced instruction working on a function built in memory. `branch_taken` is 2 when the `combat.branch` stub took the jump of a function built in memory (1: fell through). `branch2_path` / `branch2_eax`: the same for a `jcc rel8` whose next instruction (`add eax, -2`, eax = 0x28) is displaced with it. nil until it is done.

- returns `{fmul: number, fld: number, registers_kept: boolean, ability_store: integer, ability_add: integer, ability_edx: integer, ability_kept: boolean, damage: integer, effect_exit: integer, effect_entry0: integer, effect_entry1: integer, effect_counter: integer, bonus_int: integer, bonus_float: number, slot_byte: integer, branch_taken: integer, branch2_path: integer, branch2_eax: integer}?`

#### `gear.auto.object_bytes(id, offset, size) -> string?, string?`

The raw bytes of an object as lower-case hex (for self tests and reverse engineering), `size` 1 to 4096 bytes from `offset`.

- `id`: `integer`
- `offset`: `integer`
- `size`: `integer`
- returns `hex` `string?`
- returns `error` `string?`

#### `gear.auto.write(name, text) -> boolean?`

Writes a file into `GearAutomation\<instance>`.

- `name`: `string`
- `text`: `string`
- returns `ok` `boolean?`

#### `gear.auto.start_gameserver(seconds) -> integer`

Starts GameServer.exe the way the game does for a hosted LAN game (with Sacred Gear injected when mods overlay files), lets it run `seconds` (default 8) and ends it. Its logs are in the game folder (SacredGear-server.log, SacredBild-server.log).

- `seconds`: `number` (optional)
- returns `pid` `integer` - 0 if it did not start

#### `gear.auto.show_window(name, shown) -> boolean`

Shows or hides an in-game window by its control name (`UI_WND_CHEST` ...) through the window's own `show`, without the events that normally open it (the chest window opens when the hero uses a chest). For self tests; false if there is no such window.

- `name`: `string`
- `shown`: `boolean`
- returns `ok` `boolean`

#### `gear.auto.network_flag(on) -> boolean`

Sets or clears the engine's network-game flag (the byte the engine's own object and inventory code test), to test that the guards (`world.can_change`, inventory changes, `spawn`) refuse in a network game. Set it, test and clear it in the same tick: nothing else runs in between.

- `on`: `boolean`
- returns `ok` `boolean`

#### `gear.auto.network_mode(mode) -> boolean`

Sets the flags `gear.mp.mode()` reads (`'single'`, `'lan'`, `'open'`, `'closed'`; the network-game flag too), to test what depends on the kind of game without one. Read the old mode first and put it back in the same tick: nothing else runs in between.

- `mode`: `'single'|'lan'|'open'|'closed'|'internet'` - `'internet'`: the Internet menu was used and nothing is proven (reads as `'closed'`)
- returns `ok` `boolean`

#### `gear.auto.hero_from_server(on)`

Sets or clears "the game server delivered the hero" (message 0x132), the proof of Closed Net that `gear.mp.mode()` reads; set, an `'open'` game reads as `'closed'`.

- `on`: `boolean`

#### `gear.auto.chat_add(text, channel, color) -> boolean`

Adds a line to the game's message list as the game itself does (through Gear's hook: `chat.line` gets it, and a replaced overlay keeps it off the screen). In game only. For self tests of `gear.chat`.

- `text`: `string` - UTF-8, with the game's backslash codes if wanted.
- `channel`: `integer` (optional) - 1 (default) to 4, or 0x10.
- `color`: `integer` (optional) - ARGB; 0 (default): the channel's colour.
- returns `ok` `boolean`

#### `gear.auto.chat_send(kind, target, text) -> boolean`

Sends a chat message on the network as the game's chat does (a network game only): `'private'` to `target` (a slot), `'team'` or `'global'`. For self tests of `gear.chat`: a private message to the own slot goes out to the game server and comes back like another player's.

- `kind`: `'private'|'team'|'global'`
- `target`: `integer` - The slot for `'private'` (0 otherwise).
- `text`: `string` - At most 127 characters.
- returns `ok` `boolean`

#### `gear.auto.quit(code)`

Ends the game at once with that exit code.

- `code`: `integer` (optional) - Default 0.

#### `gear.auto.wait_for_menu(timeout) -> boolean`

In a task: waits until the main menu is up.

- `timeout`: `number` (optional) - Default 120.
- returns `up` `boolean`

#### `gear.auto.wait_for_game(timeout) -> boolean`

In a task: waits until a game with a hero runs.

- `timeout`: `number` (optional) - Default 180.
- returns `running` `boolean`
